steps: Android: Read minSdkVersion and the POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission in the AndroidManifest.xml.
Android: Find notification code that uses setContentTitle, setContentText or setStyle.
Android: Check the visibility setting and setPublicVersion of each notification.
Trigger each notification with test data. Look at the lock screen and at the notification list.
Look for one-time codes, message text, balances or other personal data.
tests.ex: aapt2 d permissions app.apk | grep POST_NOTIFICATIONS ; grep -rn "setContentText\|setContentTitle\|setVisibility\|setPublicVersion" out/
tests.exp: Notifications only say that an event occurred. They show no sensitive values, and the lock screen shows a redacted version.

tests.title: Check sensitive screens for overlay attack protection
tests.obj: Finds screens where a malicious app can cover or imitate the UI and steal taps.
pre: Android device with a test overlay app.
steps: Android: List the screens for login, payment approval, permission requests and security settings.
Android: Search for setFilterTouchesWhenObscured, android:filterTouchesWhenObscured and onFilterTouchEventForSecurity.
Android: Search for FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED checks in touch handlers.
Android: Read targetSdkVersion. If it is 31 or higher, look for setHideOverlayWindows and the HIDE_OVERLAY_WINDOWS permission.
Android: Draw a test overlay over each sensitive screen. Tap through it.
tests.ex: grep -rn "setFilterTouchesWhenObscured\|filterTouchesWhenObscured\|onFilterTouchEventForSecurity\|setHideOverlayWindows" out/ ; aapt2 d permissions app.apk | grep HIDE_OVERLAY_WINDOWS
tests.exp: Sensitive screens ignore touches when another window covers them. The app hides external overlays on API level 31 and higher.

tests.title: Check that sensitive views are hidden from accessibility services
tests.obj: Finds views that any accessibility service can read or control.
pre: Android 14 (API 34) or newer for the runtime part.
steps: Android: Search the layouts and code for accessibilityDataSensitive and setAccessibilityDataSensitive.
Android: Search for filterTouchesWhenObscured, because it also makes a view data sensitive.
Android: Hook the setters at runtime and use the app on every sensitive screen.
Android: Dump the UI hierarchy of each sensitive screen. Look at the isAccessibilityDataSensitive value of each view.
Android: Take a screenshot of each screen. Find the views with secrets or personal data.
tests.ex: adb shell uiautomator dump /sdcard/ui.xml ; adb pull /sdcard/ui.xml ; adb shell dumpsys activity top ; adb exec-out screencap -p > screen.png ; frida -U -f <pkg> -l hook_a11y_sensitive.js
tests.exp: Each view that shows or takes sensitive data is accessibility data sensitive. Only declared accessibility tools can read it.

tests.title: Check that screens show only the sensitive data that the task needs
tests.obj: Finds screens that show full secrets or personal data without need.
steps: Open each screen that shows card numbers, identifiers, account data or personal data.
Look for values that the app could show in part, such as the last four digits.
Check that the app shows full values only after an explicit user action.
Check that the full value hides again after a short time or when the screen closes.
tests.ex: Manual review with screenshots of each screen ; compare displayed values with the stored data
tests.exp: The app shows only the part of a sensitive value that the task needs. Full values need a user action and hide again.

tests.title: Check Android WebViews for JavaScript with local file access
tests.obj: Finds WebViews where injected script can read local files and send them out.
pre: Android device with Frida server for the runtime part.
steps: Android: Search the decompiled code for WebView, WebSettings and setJavaScriptEnabled.
Android: Read the values of setAllowFileAccess, setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs and setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs.
Android: Read minSdkVersion. Below API 30 setAllowFileAccess defaults to true. Below API 16 the two file URL settings default to true.
Android: Hook the setters at runtime to see the real values and backtraces.
Android: Find the WebViews that load file:// content or handle sensitive data.
Android: Look for a way to inject HTML or script into those WebViews.
tests.ex: jadx -d out app.apk ; grep -rn "setJavaScriptEnabled\|setAllowFileAccess\|setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs\|setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs" out/ ; frida -U -f <pkg> -l hook_websettings.js
tests.exp: No WebView enables JavaScript together with file access and file URL access. WebViews that load local content do not render untrusted content.

tests.title: Check Android WebViews for content provider access
tests.obj: Finds WebViews that let script read content providers of the app.
pre: Decompiled app code.
steps: Android: Search the decompiled code for setAllowContentAccess and setJavaScriptEnabled.
Android: Note that setAllowContentAccess defaults to true when the code does not set it.
Android: List all content providers in the AndroidManifest.xml, also those that are not exported.
Android: Hook the WebSettings setters at runtime. Record the values and backtraces.
Android: Find out if the providers hold sensitive data.
Android: Check if setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is true.
tests.ex: grep -rn "setAllowContentAccess\|setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs" out/ ; aapt2 d xmltree app.apk --file AndroidManifest.xml | grep -A8 "E: provider" ; frida -U -f <pkg> -l hook_websettings.js
tests.exp: WebViews that run JavaScript disable content access, or no content provider holds sensitive data. Universal access from file URLs stays off.

tests.title: Check JavaScript bridges between WebViews and native code
tests.obj: Finds bridges that give web content access to sensitive native functions or data.
pre: Decompiled APK and extracted IPA.
steps: Android: Search the code for addJavascriptInterface and setJavaScriptEnabled(true).
Android: Read each object that the code registers. List its public methods that have @JavascriptInterface.
iOS: Search the binary for WKUserContentController add(_:name:) and WKScriptMessageHandler classes.
iOS: Read each userContentController(_:didReceive:) method. List the actions that a message can start.
Check if a bridge method returns credentials, changes app state or runs a privileged action.
Check if the bridge checks the message input and the origin of the page.
tests.ex: jadx -d out app.apk ; grep -rn "addJavascriptInterface\|@JavascriptInterface" out/ ; r2 -A <app_binary> ; afl~WKUserContentController ; izz~addScriptMessageHandler
tests.exp: The app exposes no sensitive native function or data through a WebView bridge. Each remaining bridge checks its input and serves only trusted pages.

tests.title: Check iOS evaluateJavaScript calls for data leaks to web content
tests.obj: Finds uses of evaluateJavaScript that expose sensitive data to script in the page.
pre: Extracted IPA binary.
steps: iOS: Search the binary for evaluateJavaScript:completionHandler: and list the enclosing functions.
iOS: Find calls inside userContentController(_:didReceive:) that send bridge replies as a JavaScript callback.
iOS: Find calls that assign sensitive data to innerHTML, textContent, innerText or value.
iOS: Find calls that read DOM values, and check if they use the content world variant.
iOS: Make sure the page cannot override the callback function or read the injected DOM data.
tests.ex: r2 -A <app_binary> ; afl~evaluateJavaScript ; axt sym.imp.evaluateJavaScript ; izz~innerHTML
tests.exp: The app does not pass sensitive data to the page through evaluateJavaScript. DOM reads use an isolated content world.

tests.title: Check iOS WebViews for password fields in loaded HTML
tests.obj: Finds password inputs in web pages where script can read the typed value.
pre: Extracted IPA.
steps: iOS: Search the binary strings for type="password" and type='password'.
iOS: Check if the HTML loads into a WKWebView.
iOS: Look for a WKUserScript that sends focus to a native secure text field.
iOS: Check if third-party scripts or user content can run on the same page.
tests.ex: unzip app.ipa ; strings -a Payload/App.app/App | grep -i "type=.password" ; grep -rn "type=\"password\"" Payload/App.app/*.html
tests.exp: The app does not collect passwords in WebView HTML. If it does, a native input overlay reads the value and the page cannot read it.

tests.title: Check iOS WKWebView local file access and file origin settings
tests.obj: Finds WKWebViews where script from file URLs can read other local files.
pre: Extracted IPA; jailbroken device for the runtime part.
steps: iOS: Search the binary for loadFileURL(_:allowingReadAccessTo:). Read the readAccessURL argument of each call.
iOS: Flag read access to the whole Documents directory or the app container root.
iOS: Search for allowFileAccessFromFileURLs and allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs set with setValue:forKey:.
iOS: Hook the setting calls at runtime. Record values and backtraces.
iOS: Check if attacker-controlled input selects the loaded file or injects script.
tests.ex: r2 -A <app_binary> ; afl~loadFileURL ; izz~allowFileAccessFromFileURLs ; frida -U -f <bundle_id> -l hook_wkwebview_setvalue.js
tests.exp: The app limits readAccessURL to the one folder that it needs. Neither file origin setting is true for WebViews that load local files.

tests.title: Check that WebViews load only trusted URLs
tests.obj: Finds WebViews that open attacker-controlled or arbitrary URLs.
pre: Android device with Frida server.
steps: Android: Find setWebViewClient calls and classes that extend WebViewClient.
Android: Read shouldOverrideUrlLoading and shouldInterceptRequest. Check that they match the host against an allowlist.
Android: Hook both methods at runtime. Record the URLs and the return values.
iOS: Search for WKWebView load, loadFileURL, loadHTMLString and loadRequest calls. Trace the URL source.
iOS: Check if a deep link, a pasteboard value or a network response can set the URL.
Send the app a URL on an untrusted host and see if the WebView opens it.
tests.ex: jadx -d out app.apk ; grep -rn "shouldOverrideUrlLoading\|shouldInterceptRequest\|setWebViewClient" out/ ; frida -U -f <pkg> -l hook_webviewclient.js ; r2 -A <app_binary> ; afl~WKWebView
tests.exp: WebViews open only URLs on allowed hosts. The code checks the full host, not a substring, and external links open in the system browser.

tests.title: Check that Android SafeBrowsing stays on for WebViews
tests.obj: Finds WebViews that skip the Safe Browsing check for known bad sites.
pre: Decoded APK.
steps: Android: Read the AndroidManifest.xml for the android.webkit.WebView.EnableSafeBrowsing meta-data.
Android: Flag the value false.
Android: Search the code for WebSettings.setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false).
Android: Remember that the code setting wins over the manifest value.
tests.ex: aapt2 d xmltree app.apk --file AndroidManifest.xml | grep -B2 -A2 EnableSafeBrowsing ; grep -rn "setSafeBrowsingEnabled" out/
tests.exp: The manifest does not turn off SafeBrowsing and no code calls setSafeBrowsingEnabled with false.

tests.title: Check iOS apps for the deprecated UIWebView
tests.obj: Finds apps that use UIWebView, which has weaker isolation than WKWebView.
pre: Extracted IPA.
steps: iOS: Extract the binaries from the IPA, including frameworks.
iOS: Search all binaries for references to UIWebView.
iOS: List the third-party libraries that bring in UIWebView.
tests.ex: unzip app.ipa ; grep -rl UIWebView Payload/App.app ; r2 -A <app_binary> ; ic~UIWebView
tests.exp: No binary in the app uses UIWebView. All web content uses WKWebView.

tests.title: Check that the app cleans WebView storage with sensitive data
tests.obj: Finds WebView caches, cookies and storage that keep sensitive data after use.
pre: Android device. A debug build or root access to read the app data folder.
steps: Android: List the WebView storage settings that the app enables, such as cache, DOM storage and database.
Android: Hook the cleanup calls, such as clearCache with includeDiskFiles, and record them.
Android: Use the app with sensitive test data in the WebView. Close the app.
Android: Pull the app_webview directory from the app data folder.
Android: Search the files for the sensitive test data.
Android: Check for the cleanup of cookies and WebStorage when the user logs out.
tests.ex: adb shell run-as <pkg> ls app_webview ; adb exec-out run-as <pkg> tar c app_webview | tar x ; grep -rl "<test data>" app_webview ; frida -U -f <pkg> -l hook_webview_cleanup.js
tests.exp: The app_webview folder holds no sensitive data after the app closes. The app calls the cleanup APIs for each storage area that it enables.

tests.title: Check third-party scripts that run in WebViews
tests.obj: Finds WebView pages that load scripts from outside parties without limits.
pre: Intercepting proxy set up on the test device.
steps: List the pages that the app loads in WebViews and the remote scripts on each page.
Check if the script tags use Subresource Integrity with an integrity value.
Check if the vendor host sends CORS headers, as Subresource Integrity needs them.
Check if the page keeps third-party scripts away from sensitive fields and URL parameters.
Check if the page isolates untrusted tags in a sandboxed iframe.
Look at the vendor scripts for changes at regular times.
tests.ex: Burp Suite: proxy the WebView traffic and list the script hosts ; curl -s https://<page> | grep -i "<script" ; openssl dgst -sha384 -binary script.js | openssl base64 -A
tests.exp: Third-party scripts in WebViews carry integrity values or run in a sandbox. They cannot read sensitive page data.

tests.title: Build and check the cloud asset inventory
tests.obj: Finds resources that no one owns, tracks or patches.
steps: List all resources in every account, region and project.
Compare the list to the asset register.
Find resources without owner, environment or purpose tags.

tests.obj: Finds notebook users that can get root, a terminal or download files.
steps: List notebook instances and workbenches.
Check that root access is off.
Check if terminal access and file download are off for sensitive data.
Open a test notebook and try to get root.
tests.ex: aws sagemaker describe-notebook-instance --notebook-instance-name <n> --query RootAccess; gcloud workbench instances describe <i> --location=<l>; prowler aws --services sagemaker; prowler gcp --services vertexai
tests.exp: Users have no root access. Terminal and file download are off for sensitive data. The root test fails.

other: Microsoft cloud security benchmark v1 PA-7

tests.title: Check KMS key use, deletion state, multi-region keys and enclave attestation
tests.obj: Finds unused keys, keys set for deletion and keys with weak attestation conditions.
steps: List all keys with state and last use.
Find unused keys and keys pending deletion.
Find multi-region keys and the reason for each.
Read key policies for attestation conditions.
Check that debug mode enclaves cannot use the key.
tests.ex: aws kms list-keys; aws kms describe-key --key-id <k>; aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <k> --policy-name default; aws kms list-grants --key-id <k>; prowler aws --services kms
tests.exp: Unused keys are removed after review. No key is set for deletion without approval. Key policies need attestation and block debug enclaves.

tests.title: Check function dead letter queues and cross-account layers
tests.obj: Finds functions that lose failed events or load code layers from outside accounts.
steps: List all functions and their layers.
Find layers owned by other accounts.
Check that each async function has a dead letter queue or failure target.
Send a failing event to a test function.
tests.ex: aws lambda list-functions; aws lambda get-function --function-name <f> --query "Configuration.[Layers,DeadLetterConfig]"; prowler aws --check awslambda_function_no_dead_letter_queue awslambda_function_using_cross_account_layers
tests.exp: Layers come from trusted accounts only. Failed events go to a dead letter queue with an alert. The failing test event is stored and alerted.

tests.title: Check client certificates and cache encryption on API gateways
tests.obj: Finds API stages that send unauthenticated calls to backends or cache clear text data.
steps: List API stages.
Check that stages use a client certificate to the backend.
Check that the stage cache is encrypted.
Call the backend directly without the certificate.
tests.ex: aws apigateway get-stage --rest-api-id <id> --stage-name <s> --query "[clientCertificateId,cacheClusterEnabled]"; aws apigateway get-rest-apis; curl -i https://<backend>/; prowler aws --services apigateway
tests.exp: The backend accepts calls with the gateway certificate only. The stage cache is encrypted. The direct call is denied.

tests.title: Check container task definitions for privilege, host sharing and root file system
tests.obj: Finds tasks that run privileged, share the host or write to the root file system.
steps: List the task definitions in use.
Find privileged containers.
Find host network and host process sharing.
Check that the root file system is read-only.
Check that logging is on.
tests.ex: aws ecs list-task-definitions; aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition <t> --query "taskDefinition.[networkMode,pidMode,containerDefinitions[].[privileged,readonlyRootFilesystem]]"; prowler aws --services ecs

tests.title: Check image tag immutability and lifecycle rules in registries
tests.obj: Finds registries where a tag can point to a new image or old images pile up.
steps: List the repositories.
Check that tag immutability is on.
Check that a lifecycle policy removes old images.
Push a changed image to an existing tag in a test repository.
tests.ex: aws ecr describe-repositories --query "repositories[].[repositoryName,imageTagMutability]"; aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy --repository-name <r>; prowler aws --services ecr

Microsoft cloud security benchmark v1 AM-3

tests.title: Check database vulnerability assessment scans and reports
tests.obj: Finds databases with no recurring vulnerability scan or no report recipient.
steps: List the managed database servers.
Check that vulnerability assessment is on.
Check that scans run each week.
Check that reports go to the admins.
Open the latest report and examine the findings.
tests.ex: az sql server va-setting show -g <rg> -n <s>; az sql db threat-policy show -g <rg> -s <s> -n <d>; prowler azure --services sqlserver
tests.exp: Vulnerability assessment runs on a schedule. Reports go to the admins. Open findings have an owner and a due date.

tests.title: Review who can run and change infrastructure code
tests.obj: Finds identities with wide rights to deploy or edit infrastructure.
steps: List the people and automation roles that can apply infrastructure changes.
Check that each role has only the rights its stack needs.
Check that changes need review and a protected branch.
Check that the rights granted to created resources are limited.
tests.ex: aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name <deploy-role>; git log --merges <iac-repo>; checkov -d <iac-dir>
tests.exp: Deploy roles have limited rights per stack. Changes need review. The resources that the code creates get minimal permissions.

tests.title: Scan infrastructure code for misconfigurations before deploy
tests.obj: Finds insecure settings in templates before they reach a cloud account.
steps: Run an IaC scanner on all templates and modules.
Review high findings such as public access, open ports and missing encryption.
Check that failed checks block the merge.
Compare the scan result to the posture scan of the account.
tests.ex: checkov -d <iac-dir>; trivy config <iac-dir>; tfsec <iac-dir>
tests.exp: Templates have no high findings without a written exception. The scan gates the deploy and matches the live posture.

tests.title: Check for configuration drift and immutable infrastructure
tests.obj: Finds live resources that differ from the code, so manual changes escape review.
steps: Run a drift check of the live account against the code.
List resources that someone changed by hand.
Check who can change resources outside the pipeline.
Check that changes replace the resource and do not patch it in place.
tests.ex: terraform plan -detailed-exitcode; aws cloudformation detect-stack-drift --stack-name <s>; az deployment group what-if -g <rg> --template-file <t>
tests.exp: The live state matches the code. Manual changes are blocked or raise an alert. Changes are made by new versions of the resource.

tests.title: Check deploy-time tags, inventory and secrets handling in infrastructure code
tests.obj: Finds templates that create untagged resources or place secrets in code and state.
steps: Check that templates set owner and purpose tags on every resource.
Search templates, variables and state for secret values.
Check that secrets come from a secret store at deploy.
Check access to state files.
tests.ex: checkov -d <iac-dir>; gitleaks detect --source <iac-repo>; grep -rIiE "password|secret|key" <iac-dir>
tests.exp: Every created resource has tags and an inventory entry. Templates and state hold no secrets, and state files have limited access.

tests.title: Find over-permissive IAM roles and policies
tests.obj: Finds identities with wildcard actions or resources and more rights than their task needs.
pre: Read-only IAM audit role.
steps: Export all policies and role assignments.
Find Allow statements with * for action or resource.
List the identities that can change IAM or create roles.
Compare actual use with granted rights.
tests.ex:
aws iam get-account-authorization-details; aws accessanalyzer list-findings; az role assignment list --all; gcloud projects get-iam-policy

; prowler aws --services iam
tests.exp: No identity has wildcard admin rights without a written reason. Each role holds only the actions and resources its task needs.

tests.title: Check that workloads use short-lived identities and not stored keys
tests.obj: Finds access keys and service credentials that stay valid after a leak.
steps: List all access keys, service account keys and client secrets.
Find keys older than the policy age or never used.
Check that workloads use role-based or federated credentials.
Revoke unused keys in a test or after approval.
tests.ex: aws iam generate-credential-report; aws iam list-access-keys --user-name <u>; gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account <sa>; az ad app credential list --id <app>
tests.exp: Workloads use short-lived credentials from roles or workload identity federation. Remaining static keys are few, rotated and owned.

tests.title: Check human access: SSO, MFA and the root or owner account
tests.obj: Finds cloud accounts where people sign in with passwords alone or share admin accounts.
steps: Check that people sign in through the central identity provider.
Check that MFA is on for all console and CLI users.
Check that the root or owner account has MFA, no keys and a recovery process.
List local users and shared accounts.
tests.ex: aws iam get-account-summary; aws iam list-virtual-mfa-devices; az ad user list --query "[].userPrincipalName"; gcloud organizations get-iam-policy <org>
tests.exp: All human users sign in with SSO and MFA. The root account has no access keys and is used only for break-glass work.

tests.title: Find stale accounts, roles and external trusts
tests.obj: Finds unused identities, old roles and cross-account trusts that give unknown parties access.
steps: List identities with no sign-in or API use in the last 90 days.
List roles with trust to other accounts, external IDs or public principals.
Check each trust against the list of known partners.
Remove or restrict the entries that have no owner.
tests.ex: aws iam get-credential-report; aws iam list-roles --query "Roles[].AssumeRolePolicyDocument"; aws accessanalyzer list-analyzers; az role assignment list --all --include-inherited
tests.exp: Every identity and trust has an owner and recent use. Unused identities are removed. Trusts name specific accounts and conditions.

tests.title: Test for IAM privilege escalation paths
tests.obj: Finds identities that can raise their own rights through rights such as policy edit, role pass or key creation.
pre: Written permission and a test account.
Do not run on production.
steps: Pick a low-rights test identity.
List what it can do to IAM, compute and function resources.
Try actions that attach a stronger policy, pass a role or create a new key.
Record each path that works.
tests.ex: pacu (AWS); aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <arn> --action-names iam:PassRole iam:AttachUserPolicy
tests.exp: A low-rights identity cannot raise its rights. Rights to pass roles and edit policies are held by few admins and have conditions.

tests.title: Test microservice and cloud API endpoints for missing authentication
tests.obj: Finds internal APIs and managed service endpoints that answer without credentials.
steps: List API gateway routes, function URLs and service endpoints.
Call each one with no credentials.
Call each internal service directly, skipping the gateway.
Record each response that returns data.
tests.ex: curl -i https://<endpoint>/<path>; aws apigateway get-rest-apis; aws lambda list-function-url-configs --function-name <f>; az functionapp function show --name <f> -g <rg> -n <fn>
tests.exp: Every endpoint needs authentication and authorization. Calls without valid credentials return 401 or 403.

tests.title: List all event sources that feed code and treat each as untrusted
tests.obj: Finds event paths such as storage triggers, queues and topics that carry attacker-controlled data.
steps: List functions, workers and services that react to events.
Map each event source: API call, object upload, queue, topic, IoT message or schedule.
Mark which fields an outside party controls, such as object names and metadata.
Rank sources by exposure.
tests.ex: aws lambda list-event-source-mappings; aws s3api get-bucket-notification-configuration --bucket <b>; gcloud eventarc triggers list; az eventgrid topic list
tests.exp: Every event source is listed with its owner and the fields that outside parties control. Each handler validates these fields.

tests.title: Send crafted values through event fields to the handlers
tests.obj: Finds handlers that pass event data into commands, queries or templates without checks.
pre: Use a test environment.
Do not run on production.
steps: Create a test object with a name that holds shell and SQL meta characters.
Send a queue message with the same values in each field.
Watch the handler logs and downstream systems for errors or changed behavior.
Send oversize, wrong type and extra fields.
tests.ex: aws s3 cp test.txt "s3://<b>/a;id;.txt"; aws sqs send-message --queue-url <q> --message-body "{\"id\":\"1 OR 1=1\"}"; gcloud pubsub topics publish <t> --message "<payload>"
tests.exp: Handlers reject or neutralize malformed values. No command runs, no query changes, and errors show no internals.

tests.title: Check input validation, parameterized access and least rights in handlers
tests.obj: Finds handler code that builds queries or commands from event data, with roles that make the damage worse.
steps: Read the handler code for string-built queries and shell calls.
Check for allow-list validation of type, length and format.
Check that data access uses parameterized calls.
Check that the handler role cannot reach other data.
tests.ex: semgrep --config auto <handler-dir>; grep -rnE "os.system|subprocess|exec\(|eval\(" <handler-dir>
tests.exp: Handlers validate input with allow-lists and use parameterized access. The role limits the damage of a flaw.

tests.title: Check message and event integrity in queues, topics and buses
tests.obj: Finds messaging systems where any writer can inject events that other services trust.
steps: List who can publish to each queue, topic and event bus.
Check the access policies for public or wide principals.
Publish a forged event with a test identity that has no rights.
Check that consumers check the source and format.
tests.ex: aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url <q> --attribute-names Policy; aws sns get-topic-attributes --topic-arn <t>; gcloud pubsub topics get-iam-policy <t>
tests.exp: Only named producers can publish. Consumers check source and message format, and a forged message is rejected.

tests.title: Check that audit logs are on in every account and region
tests.obj: Finds accounts and regions where cloud API activity leaves no record.
steps: List all accounts, subscriptions, projects and regions in use.
Check that the audit trail is on for each, with management and data events.
Make a test change and find its record.
Check that the record shows identity, source address and time.
tests.ex: aws cloudtrail describe-trails; aws cloudtrail get-trail-status --name <t>; az monitor diagnostic-settings subscription list; gcloud logging sinks list
tests.exp: Audit logs cover all accounts and regions. The test change appears with identity, source address and time.

tests.title: Check protection and retention of cloud logs
tests.obj: Finds logs that an attacker with account access can edit or delete.
steps: Find the storage target of each log source.
Check that the target is in a separate account with write-once or locked storage.
Check who can delete or change the logs and the log settings.
Check the retention time against the rules.
tests.ex: aws cloudtrail get-trail --name <t> --query Trail.LogFileValidationEnabled; aws s3api get-object-lock-configuration --bucket <b>; gcloud logging buckets list
tests.exp: Logs go to a separate protected store with integrity checks. Few identities can change or delete logs, and retention meets the rules.

tests.title: Check network flow, DNS and load balancer logs
tests.obj: Finds networks where traffic between services and to the Internet cannot be traced.
steps: List VPCs, subnets and load balancers.
Check that flow logs, DNS logs and access logs are on.
Make a test connection between two services.
Find it in the logs.
tests.ex: aws ec2 describe-flow-logs; az network watcher flow-log list -l <region>; gcloud compute networks subnets describe <s> --format="value(logConfig)"
tests.exp: Flow, DNS and load balancer logs are on for all networks. The test connection appears in the log.

tests.title: Test alerts for security events and cost or usage anomalies
tests.obj: Finds environments where known attack steps raise no alert.
pre: Use a test account.
steps: List the alert rules for sign-in, IAM change, log change, key use and storage policy change.
Do a test action for each rule in a test account.
Check that the alert reaches the response team.
Check alerts for unusual usage of compute, functions, databases and cost.
tests.ex: aws cloudwatch describe-alarms; aws events list-rules; aws budgets describe-budgets --account-id <id>; az monitor activity-log alert list; gcloud alpha monitoring policies list
tests.exp: Each test action raises an alert in the agreed time. Alerts for usage and cost anomalies exist and have an owner.

tests.title: Check that logs hold no secrets and that time sources agree
tests.obj: Finds logs that expose credentials or cannot be matched across systems.
steps: Search sample logs of functions, gateways and agents for tokens and keys.
Check the field list against the log standard.
Compare timestamps of one request across three systems.
Check the time sync setting of the hosts.
tests.ex: grep -rIiE "password|token|secret|authorization" <log-sample>; compare timestamps of one correlation ID
tests.exp: Logs hold no credentials or protected personal data. Timestamps agree and every record carries a correlation ID.

tests.title: Check the network is split into frontend, middleware and backend zones
tests.obj: Finds flat networks where a breach of a web server gives direct access to databases and key stores.
steps: Get the network diagram and the list of VPCs and subnets.
Map each system to a zone: frontend, middleware or backend.
Check the rules between zones and the allowed flows.
From a frontend host, try to reach a backend host.
tests.ex: aws ec2 describe-subnets; aws ec2 describe-route-tables; az network vnet list; gcloud compute networks subnets list; nmap -Pn -p <db-port> <backend-host>
tests.exp: Frontend hosts cannot reach backend systems directly. Each flow between zones is allowed by a written rule.

tests.title: Find internal services that the Internet can reach
tests.obj: Finds microservices, admin tools and queues exposed by load balancers, public IPs or function URLs.
pre: Written approval for the scan of the listed addresses.
steps: List all public IP addresses, load balancers and public endpoints.
Map each one to a service and an owner.
Scan the public addresses for open ports.
Mark each endpoint that is not meant to be public.
tests.ex: aws ec2 describe-addresses; aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --query "LoadBalancers[?Scheme==\`internet-facing\`]"; az network public-ip list; gcloud compute addresses list; nmap -sV <ip>
tests.exp: Only reviewed edge services are public. Internal services use private addresses or private endpoints.

tests.title: Check egress filtering and monitoring of traffic to unknown domains
tests.obj: Finds workloads that can send data to any Internet host with no record.
steps: List egress routes, NAT gateways and egress firewall rules.
From a test workload, connect to an unlisted external domain.
Check for DNS and flow logs of the connection.
Check for an alert on traffic to unknown or bad domains.
tests.ex: aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways; aws network-firewall list-firewalls; curl -m 3 https://example.org (from a test workload); query flow logs for the connection
tests.exp: Egress is limited to approved destinations. The test connection fails or raises an alert, and flow logs show the connection.

tests.title: Check hardening of the instance metadata service
tests.obj: Finds compute resources whose metadata service gives role credentials to any local process or to SSRF.
steps: List all VMs and nodes with their metadata settings.
Find resources that allow the old metadata version without a session token.
Check the hop limit for container hosts.
From a test workload, request the metadata address.
tests.ex: aws ec2 describe-instances --query "Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,MetadataOptions.HttpTokens,MetadataOptions.HttpPutResponseHopLimit]"; curl -m 3 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (test host)
tests.exp: All compute resources require session-token metadata access (IMDSv2) and the old version is off. Workloads cannot read role credentials without a token.

tests.title: Check TLS and authentication on traffic between services
tests.obj: Finds east-west traffic that is plaintext or accepts any caller.
steps: List the service-to-service connections from the diagram.
Capture traffic between two test services.
Check for TLS and for mutual authentication or signed tokens.
Send a call with no valid identity.
tests.ex: tcpdump -i any -A port <port> (test hosts); openssl s_client -connect <svc>:<port>; curl -v http://<svc>:<port>
tests.exp: Service traffic uses TLS with mutual authentication or validated signed tokens. A call with no valid identity is rejected.

tests.title: Check WAF and DDoS protection at internet-facing endpoints
tests.obj: Finds public endpoints with no web filter or protection against traffic floods.
steps: List all internet-facing applications and CDNs.
Check that a WAF with managed rules is attached to each.
Check custom rules for sensitive routes and rate limits.
Check that DDoS protection is on based on the risk of the application.
tests.ex: aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope REGIONAL; aws shield describe-subscription; az network application-gateway waf-policy list; gcloud compute security-policies list
tests.exp: Each public application has a WAF in block mode with custom rules and rate limits. DDoS protection follows the application risk.

tests.title: Check service quotas and budget limits per account
tests.obj: Finds accounts where one resource or attacker can use up quotas or run up large cost.
steps: List service quotas and current use for compute, storage and network.
Check budget limits and cost alerts for each account.
Check who can raise quotas or create large resources.
Check for alerts when use passes a set share of the limit.
tests.ex: aws service-quotas list-service-quotas --service-code ec2; aws budgets describe-budgets --account-id <id>; az consumption budget list; gcloud alpha billing budgets list --billing-account <id>
tests.exp: Each account has quotas and budgets with alerts. Few identities can raise quotas or create large resources.

tests.title: Test rate limits and throttling on public APIs and gateways
tests.obj: Finds gateways that accept unlimited requests from one caller.
pre: Use a test environment.
Do not run on production.
steps: List the rate and burst settings of each gateway stage and route.
Send requests above the limit from one test client.
Check that the gateway returns a throttling response.
Check that limits apply per caller, not only in total.
tests.ex: aws apigateway get-usage-plans; hey -n 1000 -c 50 https://<api>/<path>; az apim api show; gcloud api-gateway api-configs list
tests.exp: Each route has rate and burst limits per caller. Requests above the limit get HTTP 429 and the backend stays healthy.

tests.title: Check autoscaling limits and scale-out protection
tests.obj: Finds autoscaling groups with no upper limit or with no alert, so a flood causes cost and instability.
steps: List autoscaling groups, container services and function settings.
Find groups with no maximum size.
Check the metrics and alarms that start scale-out.
Check that scale limits match the budget.
tests.ex: aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --query "AutoScalingGroups[].[AutoScalingGroupName,MaxSize]"; az monitor autoscale list -g <rg>; gcloud compute instance-groups managed list
tests.exp: Every scaling group has a maximum size that fits the budget, with alarms for scale-out events.

tests.title: Check CPU, memory and storage limits on cloud container services
tests.obj: Finds container tasks and VM workloads with no resource limits.
steps: List container tasks, jobs and services.
Check the CPU and memory limits in each definition.
Find tasks with no limit.
Check the disk and log growth limits.
tests.ex: aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition <t> --query "taskDefinition.[cpu,memory]"; az container show -n <c> -g <rg> --query containers[].resources; gcloud run services describe <s>
tests.exp: Every container task sets CPU and memory limits and storage and log growth limits.

tests.title: Check access control and audit records of the cloud secret store
tests.obj: Finds secret stores where many identities can read all secrets and reads leave no record.
steps: List the identities that can read, write or delete secrets.
Check that each workload can read only its own secrets.
Read a test secret and find the audit record.
Check for an alert when a secret is read from an unexpected source.
tests.ex: aws secretsmanager list-secrets; aws secretsmanager get-resource-policy --secret-id <id>; az keyvault show -n <v> --query properties.enableRbacAuthorization; gcloud secrets get-iam-policy <s>; query the audit log for the read event
tests.exp: Access is scoped per secret and per workload. Each read is logged with identity and source, and unusual reads raise an alert.

tests.title: Find secrets in function settings, instance data and environment variables
tests.obj: Finds credentials stored in platform configuration where many readers and tools can see them.
steps: List environment variables of functions, containers and VM templates.
List instance user data and startup scripts.
Search them for passwords, tokens and keys.
Check that code fetches secrets from a vault at run time.
tests.ex: aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name <f> --query Environment; aws ec2 describe-instance-attribute --instance-id <i> --attribute userData; az functionapp config appsettings list; gcloud functions describe <f>
tests.exp: Platform configuration holds no secret values. Code fetches secrets at run time from a secret store with a short-lived identity.

tests.title: Check secret rotation, expiry and revocation
tests.obj: Finds credentials that never rotate and so stay valid after a leak.
steps: List secrets with their creation and last rotation date.
Find secrets that exceed the rotation period.
Check that rotation runs automatically.
Revoke a test secret and check that its use fails.
tests.ex: aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id <id> --query "[RotationEnabled,LastRotatedDate]"; az keyvault secret list --vault-name <v> --query "[].attributes.expires"; gcloud secrets versions list <s>
tests.exp: Secrets rotate on a set schedule and carry an expiry date. A revoked secret stops working in the agreed time.

tests.title: Check key management and envelope encryption for stored data
tests.obj: Finds keys with broad use rights, no rotation or no separation from the data owners.
steps: List the encryption keys and their policies.
Find keys that many identities can use or manage.
Check key rotation settings.
Check that key administration and key use are held by different roles.
tests.ex: aws kms list-keys; aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <k> --policy-name default; aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <k>; az keyvault key list --vault-name <v>; gcloud kms keys list --keyring <r> --location <l>
tests.exp: Keys have narrow policies, automatic rotation, and separate roles for administration and use.

tests.title: Scan repositories, storage and images for secrets
tests.obj: Finds credentials that leaked into code, buckets, logs or images.
steps: Scan the repositories and their history for secrets.
Scan storage buckets for key files, backups and config files.
Scan images and logs for tokens.
Revoke and rotate each credential found.
tests.ex: gitleaks detect --source <repo>; trufflehog git file://<repo>; trivy image --scanners secret <image>; aws s3 sync s3://<b> ./copy (scan the copy)
tests.exp: No live credential is found. Each credential found is revoked and rotated, and its source is fixed.

tests.title: Check that each function has its own minimal role
tests.obj: Finds functions that share a broad role and so give a breach the rights of many functions.
steps: List all functions and their execution roles.
Find roles that more than one function shares.
Find roles with wildcard actions or resources.
Compare the role actions to the actions in the function code.
tests.ex: aws lambda list-functions --query "Functions[].[FunctionName,Role]"; aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name <r>; gcloud functions list --format="value(name,serviceAccountEmail)"; az functionapp identity show -n <f> -g <rg>
tests.exp: Each function has a separate role with only the actions and resources it needs. No wildcard policy is attached.

tests.title: Check authentication on every function trigger
tests.obj: Finds triggers that let anyone invoke a function or feed it events.
steps: List all triggers: API gateways, function URLs, queues, topics, buckets and schedules.
Check the authorizer or access policy of each trigger.
Invoke each public trigger without credentials.
Check the resource policy for public principals.
tests.ex: aws lambda get-policy --function-name <f>; aws lambda get-function-url-config --function-name <f>; curl -i https://<function-url>; gcloud functions get-iam-policy <f>
tests.exp: Every trigger needs authentication and authorization. Resource policies allow only named principals, and a call without credentials fails.

tests.title: Check network isolation and egress of functions
tests.obj: Finds functions with unneeded Internet access or access to internal networks.
steps: List functions with VPC or network settings.
Find functions in the default network or with open egress.
Check that sensitive functions sit in a separate network from general functions.
From a test function, connect to an unlisted host.
tests.ex: aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name <f> --query VpcConfig; gcloud functions describe <f> --format="value(vpcConnector,ingressSettings)"; az functionapp vnet-integration list -n <f> -g <rg>
tests.exp: Functions that need no Internet access have none. Sensitive functions run in private subnets with controlled egress.

tests.title: Check execution context reuse and temporary storage
tests.obj: Finds functions that keep secrets or user data in global variables or /tmp between calls.
pre: Use a test build only.
steps: Read the function code for global variables that hold secrets or user data.
Call the function twice with different test users.
Check /tmp and memory for data from the first call.
Check for use of single-use environments for sensitive functions.
tests.ex: Code review of global and static variables; invoke the function with two test identities and print the /tmp listing in a test build
tests.exp: No secret or user data persists between calls. Code reads secrets fresh and clears temporary files.

tests.title: Check function-to-function calls and chaining
tests.obj: Finds functions that call other functions with no caller proof, so a breach can trigger the whole chain.
steps: Map which functions invoke other functions.
Check that each call uses a workload identity or a signed token.
Check that the callee checks the caller identity.
Check which role may invoke which function.
tests.ex: aws lambda list-event-source-mappings; aws lambda get-policy --function-name <f>; gcloud functions get-iam-policy <f>
tests.exp: Function calls are authenticated with workload identity or signed tokens. Each function allows only named callers.

tests.title: Check concurrency limits and throttling for functions
tests.obj: Finds functions that can scale without bound and cause cost or denial of service.
steps: List concurrency and timeout settings of each function.
Find functions with no reserved or maximum concurrency.
Check API gateway throttling in front of them.
Check the cost alerts for function invocations.
tests.ex: aws lambda get-function-concurrency --function-name <f>; aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name <f> --query Timeout; aws apigateway get-stages --rest-api-id <id>
tests.exp: Functions have concurrency and timeout limits. Gateways throttle callers, and cost and invocation alerts exist.

tests.title: Check cloud container registries for access, source and transport
tests.obj: Finds registries that allow anonymous or wide push and pull, or that accept images from untrusted sources.
steps: List the container registries and repositories.
Check the access policy for each repository.
Try an anonymous pull and push.
Check that only the build system can push and that transfers use TLS.
tests.ex: aws ecr describe-repositories; aws ecr get-repository-policy --repository-name <r>; az acr list; az acr repository list -n <acr>; gcloud artifacts repositories list
tests.exp: Registries need authentication. Only build identities can push, pull rights follow need, and all transfers use TLS.

tests.title: Check that only trusted and current images run in cloud services
tests.obj: Finds services that run untrusted, unsigned or stale images.
steps: List images used by container services and functions.
Find images from public or unknown sources.
Check the age of each image and its last rebuild.
Check the rule that blocks untrusted images at deploy.
tests.ex: aws ecs list-task-definitions; aws lambda list-functions --query "Functions[?PackageType==\`Image\`]"; az containerapp list; gcloud run services list
tests.exp: Services run only images from approved registries with known digests. Images are rebuilt on a set schedule.

tests.title: Check patching of self-managed hosts, images and managed service versions
tests.obj: Finds VMs, machine images and managed services that run versions with known flaws.
steps: List VM images, instance OS versions and managed service engine versions.
Compare them to the current advisories and support dates.
Check the patch and image rebuild process.
Find services at end of life.
tests.ex: aws ssm describe-instance-patch-states; aws inspector2 list-findings; az vm list -d; gcloud compute images list; aws rds describe-db-instances --query "DBInstances[].[DBInstanceIdentifier,EngineVersion]"
tests.exp: Hosts and images are patched on a set schedule. No service runs an unsupported version without a written plan.

tests.title: Check vulnerability scanning for cloud workloads and dependencies
tests.obj: Finds workloads that run vulnerable libraries or images that no scan covers.
steps: List all workloads: VMs, containers and functions.
Check that each has a scan for images, packages and dependencies.
Review open findings for age and exposure.
Check the process to fix or accept each finding.
tests.ex: trivy image <image>; trivy fs <path>; grype <image>; aws inspector2 list-findings; dependency-check --scan <path>
tests.exp: All workloads have regular scans. High findings are fixed in the agreed time or accepted in writing.

tests.title: Check that users sign in through an external identity provider
tests.obj: Finds clusters where human users rely on built-in credentials with no revocation or audit.
steps: List the authentication methods in use on the API server.
Check that users authenticate through OIDC or the managed cloud identity service.
Find static token files, basic auth files and long-lived client certificates for users.
Check that the identity provider enforces MFA.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep -E "oidc|token-auth-file|client-ca"; kubectl config view --raw | grep -E "client-certificate|token"
tests.exp: Users sign in with short-lived tokens from an external identity provider with MFA. No static token file exists and no user certificates are valid for years.

tests.title: Check that anonymous API access is off or has no rights
tests.obj: Finds API servers that serve anonymous requests with rights.
steps: Send a request to the API without credentials.
Send requests to resource paths as system:anonymous.
List ClusterRoleBindings for system:anonymous and system:unauthenticated.
On self-managed clusters, read the anonymous-auth flag.
tests.ex: curl -k https://<api>:6443/api/v1/namespaces; curl -k https://<api>:6443/version; kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json | jq ".items[] | select(.subjects[]?.name | IN(\"system:anonymous\",\"system:unauthenticated\"))"
tests.exp: Requests with no credentials get HTTP 401 or 403. No role grants rights to system:anonymous or system:unauthenticated beyond the minimum.

tests.title: Check that service account tokens are not used outside the cluster
tests.obj: Finds long-lived service account tokens that people or external systems use.
steps: Find Secrets of type service-account-token.
Search the audit log for requests from service accounts with source IPs outside the cluster.
Check CI and external tools for stored cluster tokens.
Check the expiry of each token.
tests.ex: kubectl get secrets -A --field-selector type=kubernetes.io/service-account-token; kubectl create token <sa> --duration 1h
tests.exp: No external system uses a long-lived service account token. External tools use short-lived tokens from TokenRequest or a federated identity.

tests.title: Check use of client certificates for user access
tests.obj: Finds user client certificates that cannot be revoked and last for a long time.
steps: List user kubeconfig entries that use client certificates.
Check the validity period of each certificate.
Check the break-glass process for certificate use.
Check that the cluster CA is not shared between environments.
tests.ex: openssl x509 -in <client.crt> -noout -dates -subject; kubectl get csr
tests.exp: User client certificates are used only for break-glass access. They are short-lived, listed, and the process to re-key the cluster is documented.

tests.title: Check that kubelets reject anonymous requests
tests.obj: Finds kubelets that accept unauthenticated calls and so allow command execution on pods.
pre: Network access to a test node.
steps: Send a request to port 10250 of a node without credentials.
Send a request to the read-only port 10255.
Read the kubelet configuration for anonymous auth and authorization mode.
Check that webhook authorization is on.
tests.ex: curl -k https://<node>:10250/pods; curl http://<node>:10255/pods; grep -A3 -E "anonymous|authorization" /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
tests.exp: The kubelet returns 401 or 403 for anonymous requests. Anonymous auth is off, authorization mode is Webhook, and port 10255 is closed.

tests.title: Check that nodes join the cluster only with controlled credentials
tests.obj: Finds clusters where an unknown host can join as a node and gain access to workloads.
steps: List the bootstrap tokens and their expiry.
Check the approval rules for certificate signing requests from nodes.
Test a join with an expired token.
tests.ex: kubeadm token list; kubectl get csr; kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep authorization-mode
tests.exp: Bootstrap tokens expire in a short time. Node certificate requests need approval, and unknown hosts cannot join the cluster.

tests.title: Run a hardening scan on the cluster components
tests.obj: Finds control plane and node settings that stay on weak defaults.
steps: Run a configuration benchmark tool against the control plane and nodes.
List all failed checks with the component name.
Rank the failed checks by risk for this cluster.
Record accepted deviations with an owner.
tests.ex: kube-bench run; kubescape scan; trivy k8s --report summary cluster
tests.exp: Failed checks are fixed or have an accepted reason with an owner. API server, controller manager, scheduler, kubelet and etcd settings are hardened.

tests.title: Check that Kubernetes and its components are on a supported release
tests.obj: Finds clusters on end-of-life versions that no longer get security fixes.
steps: Get the version of the API server, kubelets and kube-proxy.
Compare each to the list of supported releases.
Check the patch level against the latest security fixes.
Check the upgrade plan and the owner.
tests.ex: kubectl version; kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,KUBELET:.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion,RUNTIME:.status.nodeInfo.containerRuntimeVersion
tests.exp: All components run a supported release with current patches. A dated upgrade plan exists for any component that is behind.

tests.title: Check patch level of the container runtime and the node kernel
tests.obj: Finds nodes with known container escape or kernel privilege escalation flaws.
steps: List the runtime and kernel versions on all nodes.
Compare them to the current security advisories for the runtime, runc and the kernel.
Check the node image age.
Check the process to replace or patch nodes.
tests.ex: kubectl get nodes -o wide; uname -r; runc --version; containerd --version; trivy rootfs / (on the node)
tests.exp: Runtime, runc and kernel have no open known critical flaws. Nodes are replaced or patched on a set schedule.

tests.title: Check hardening of the node operating system
tests.obj: Finds general-purpose node images that carry many unneeded services and packages.
steps: List the node operating system and image for each node pool.
Check if the image is a minimal container-focused OS.
List the services and packages on a sample node.
Check the firewall rules and local accounts of the node.
tests.ex: kubectl get nodes -o wide; systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running; ss -tlnp
tests.exp: Nodes use a minimal OS image with few services. Firewall rules are strict, and no unneeded packages are present.

tests.title: Check API server flags for admission control and secure access
tests.obj: Finds API server settings that turn off protections for requests and objects.
steps: Read the command line of the API server.
Check that the list of enabled admission plugins has no disabled security plugins.
Check the TLS settings and the anonymous-auth flag.
Check the audit and authorization flags.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep -E "enable-admission|disable-admission|anonymous-auth|tls-"; kube-bench run --targets master
tests.exp: The API server has no disabled security plugins, anonymous auth is off, and the TLS settings are strong.

tests.title: Build an inventory of clusters, namespaces, workloads and owners
tests.obj: Finds unknown, abandoned or unowned clusters, namespaces and workloads that nobody patches.
steps: List all clusters of the organization from the cloud accounts.
List namespaces and workloads in each cluster with owner labels.
Find workloads with no owner or with no recent deploy.
Compare the result to the asset register.
tests.ex: aws eks list-clusters; az aks list; gcloud container clusters list; kubectl get ns --show-labels; kubectl get deploy -A -o wide
tests.exp: Every cluster, namespace and workload is in the asset register with an owner. Abandoned items are removed.

tests.title: Check that the Docker daemon socket is not exposed
tests.obj: Finds hosts and containers where access to the Docker API gives root on the host.
steps: Check if the daemon listens on a TCP port.
Check the permissions and group members of /var/run/docker.sock.
List containers that mount the socket, also with a read-only flag.
Check if remote API access uses TLS and client certificates.
tests.ex: ss -tlnp | grep dockerd; ls -l /var/run/docker.sock; docker ps -q | xargs docker inspect --format "{{.Name}} {{.Mounts}}" | grep docker.sock
tests.exp: The daemon does not listen on unencrypted TCP. No container mounts the socket. Access to the socket is limited to named admins.

tests.title: Check that Docker hosts use rootless mode or user namespace remapping
tests.obj: Finds daemons and containers where root in the container is root on the host.
steps: Check if the daemon runs in rootless mode.
If not, read the userns-remap setting.
Run id inside a container and compare it to the host user.
Check the limits of rootless mode for the workload.
tests.ex: docker info --format "{{.SecurityOptions}}"; cat /etc/docker/daemon.json; docker run --rm alpine id
tests.exp: The daemon runs rootless or with user namespace remapping, and container root maps to an unprivileged host user.

tests.title: Check published ports, firewall rules and container connectivity
tests.obj: Finds container ports open on all interfaces and containers that talk to each other with no limit.
steps: List published ports for each container.
Find ports bound to 0.0.0.0 that need only local access.
Check the host firewall for rules that the container runtime bypasses.
List the Docker networks and the containers on each.
tests.ex: docker ps --format "{{.Names}} {{.Ports}}"; docker network ls; docker network inspect bridge; iptables -S DOCKER-USER
tests.exp: Ports bind to 127.0.0.1 unless public use is needed. Containers share a user-defined network only when they must talk to each other.

tests.title: Check resource limits and restart policy on containers
tests.obj: Finds containers that can use all memory, CPU, processes or restarts on a host.
pre: Do not run the stress test on production.
steps: List memory, CPU, pids and ulimit settings of each container.
Find containers with no limit.
Check the restart policy and the maximum restart count.
Run a stress test in a test container.
tests.ex: docker inspect --format "{{.Name}} {{.HostConfig.Memory}} {{.HostConfig.CpuShares}} {{.HostConfig.PidsLimit}} {{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy}}" $(docker ps -q); docker stats --no-stream
tests.exp: Each container has memory, CPU and process limits and a bounded restart policy. A stress test does not harm other containers.

tests.title: Check Docker secrets and build-time secret handling
tests.obj: Finds secrets in image layers, build arguments and container environments.
steps: Search Dockerfiles for ARG, ENV or COPY that handle credentials.
Run docker history on each image.
Check if builds use BuildKit secret mounts.
Check that runtime secrets use Docker secrets or an external store.
tests.ex: docker history --no-trunc <image>; grep -nE "ARG|ENV" Dockerfile | grep -iE "pass|token|key|secret"; docker build --secret id=mysecret,src=./secret.txt .
tests.exp: Images hold no secrets in layers, ARG or ENV. Builds use secret mounts and runtime secrets come from a managed store.

tests.title: Check the Docker daemon log level and host benchmark results
tests.obj: Finds Docker hosts with debug logging or other weak daemon settings.
steps: Read the log-level setting in daemon.json and the dockerd command line.
Run a Docker host benchmark tool.
List failed checks.
Fix or record each failed check.
tests.ex: cat /etc/docker/daemon.json; ps aux | grep "[d]ockerd"; docker-bench-security
tests.exp: The daemon log level is info unless debug is needed for a short time. Failed benchmark checks are fixed or recorded with an owner.

tests.title: Check that the API server is not open to the Internet
tests.obj: Finds API servers that any host on the Internet can reach.
pre: Written approval for the scan of the listed addresses.
steps: Find the public address of the API server from DNS, kubeconfig and cloud settings.
Connect to port 6443 from an outside network.
Read the authorized network list of the managed service.
Make sure only trusted source ranges are allowed.
tests.ex: nmap -p 6443 <api-host>; curl -k https://<api-host>:6443/version; aws eks describe-cluster --name <c> --query cluster.resourcesVpcConfig; az aks show -n <c> -g <rg> --query apiServerAccessProfile; gcloud container clusters describe <c> --format="value(masterAuthorizedNetworksConfig)"
tests.exp: The API server is reachable only from trusted networks or a private endpoint. An outside host cannot connect to port 6443.

tests.title: Check version and certificate details that the API shows to outsiders
tests.obj: Finds information leaks from the version endpoint and from certificate names.
steps: Send an unauthenticated request to the /version path.
Read the Subject Alternative Names of the API server certificate.
Look for private addresses and internal host names in the SAN list.
Check if the response gives the exact release.
tests.ex: curl -k https://<api-host>:6443/version; openssl s_client -connect <api-host>:6443 </dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -ext subjectAltName
tests.exp: The version path is not reachable from outside or needs authentication. The certificate shows no private addresses or internal names.

tests.title: Check that kubelet and etcd ports are closed to untrusted hosts
tests.obj: Finds node and control plane ports that expose the kubelet, etcd or other components.
pre: Written approval for the scan of the listed addresses.
steps: List the open ports on a control plane node and a worker node from a pod network host.
Check that only the API server can reach the kubelet and etcd.
Compare the result with the firewall and security group rules.
tests.ex: nmap -p 2379,2380,6443,10248-10260,30000-32767 <node-ip>; kubectl get nodes -o wide
tests.exp: Only the API server and named hosts reach the kubelet and etcd ports. Read-only kubelet port 10255 is closed.

tests.title: Check that etcd needs client certificates and is isolated
tests.obj: Finds etcd servers that accept unauthenticated clients or serve other components.
steps: Try to connect to etcd without a client certificate.
Check the etcd peer and client TLS settings.
Check that only API servers hold etcd client certificates.
Check that no other component uses the main etcd keyspace.
tests.ex: etcdctl --endpoints=https://<etcd>:2379 get / --prefix --keys-only; ps aux | grep etcd | tr " " "\n" | grep -E "client-cert-auth|peer-client-cert-auth"
tests.exp: An etcd request with no valid client certificate fails. Only the API servers can connect, and etcd is behind a firewall.

tests.title: Find exposed dashboards and web UIs for cluster management
tests.obj: Finds management web interfaces that give cluster rights to outsiders or to anyone in the network.
steps: List Services and Ingresses for dashboard, monitoring and admin tools.
Open each address from an untrusted network.
Check the rights of the service account of each tool.
Check that an authenticating proxy sits in front.
tests.ex: kubectl get svc,ingress -A | grep -iE "dashboard|admin|grafana|prometheus|argo"; kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o wide | grep -i dashboard
tests.exp: No management interface is public without strong authentication. The service account of each tool has minimal rights.

tests.title: Check NodePort and LoadBalancer services for unwanted exposure
tests.obj: Finds internal services that are public through NodePort or cloud load balancers.
steps: List all Services of type NodePort and LoadBalancer.
Check the source ranges and security groups of each.
Check the nodes for services in the 30000-32767 range.
Ask the owner to justify each public service.
tests.ex: kubectl get svc -A -o wide | grep -E "NodePort|LoadBalancer"; nmap -p 30000-32767 <node-ip>
tests.exp: Only reviewed services are public. Other services use ClusterIP, and each public service has restricted source ranges.

tests.title: Check that Node.js images hold only production dependencies and set NODE_ENV
tests.obj: Finds Node.js images with development packages and with non-production framework settings.
steps: Read the Dockerfile of each Node.js image.
Make sure the install step uses npm ci with the omit=dev option.
Make sure the final image sets NODE_ENV to production.
List the packages in the final image and look for development packages.
tests.ex: grep -nE "npm (ci|install)|NODE_ENV" Dockerfile; docker run --rm IMAGE npm ls --omit=prod --depth=0
tests.exp: The final image has no devDependencies. NODE_ENV is production.

tests.title: Check .dockerignore for secrets and local node_modules
tests.obj: Finds Docker builds that copy credentials or modified local packages into the image.
steps: Find the .dockerignore file next to each Dockerfile.
Make sure it lists node_modules, .env files, credential files, .npmrc and logs.
Build the image and list the files in the application folder.
Make sure no ignored file is in the image.
tests.ex: cat .dockerignore; docker build -t test . && docker run --rm test ls -la /usr/src/app
tests.exp: The .dockerignore file excludes secrets and local dependencies. The built image holds none of them.

tests.title: Check signal handling and graceful shutdown of the container process
tests.obj: Finds containers where the application misses stop signals and ends in an abrupt kill.
pre: Use a test container.
steps: Read the CMD instruction. Make sure it uses the exec form and starts node directly, not npm or a shell.
Make sure an init process such as dumb-init runs as PID 1.
Start a test container and send SIGTERM with docker kill.
Start a slow request and send the signal. Make sure the application finishes it and closes connections before it ends.
tests.ex: docker kill --signal=SIGTERM CONTAINER; curl -m 90 http://localhost:3000/slow
tests.exp: The application receives SIGTERM and SIGINT, finishes active requests and then ends.

tests.title: Check file modes of control plane manifests and kubeconfig files
tests.obj: Finds control plane files that other local users can read or change.
pre: Shell access to a control plane node.
steps: List the static pod manifests of the API server, controller manager, scheduler and etcd.
Read the mode and owner of each manifest file.
Read the mode and owner of admin.conf, scheduler.conf and controller-manager.conf.
List the kubeconfig files of administrators on the control plane nodes and read their modes.
Make sure the owner is root and no group or other user can write.
tests.ex: stat -c "%a %U:%G %n" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml /etc/kubernetes/*.conf; ls -l $HOME/.kube; kube-bench run --targets master
tests.exp: Each manifest and component kubeconfig file has the mode 600 or stricter and the owner root:root. Other users cannot read administrator kubeconfig files.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Kubeconfig Files

tests.title: Check PKI files and the etcd data directory for open access
tests.obj: Finds certificate keys and etcd data that local users can read.
pre: Shell access to a control plane node.
steps: List the files in the Kubernetes PKI directory with mode and owner.
Make sure all key files have the mode 600 and the owner root.
Find the client CA file of the API server and the kubelet and read its mode and owner.
Find the etcd data directory in the etcd flags and read its mode and owner.
Make sure only the etcd user can read the data directory.
tests.ex: stat -c "%a %U:%G %n" /etc/kubernetes/pki/* /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/*; ps -ef | grep etcd | grep -- --data-dir
tests.exp: PKI files are owned by root with the mode 600 for keys and 600 or stricter for certificates. The etcd data directory has the mode 700 and an etcd owner.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Etcd

tests.title: Check file modes of kubelet, kube-proxy and CNI files on nodes
tests.obj: Finds node configuration files that local users can change.
pre: Shell access to a worker node.
steps: Find the kubelet service file, kubelet.conf and the kubelet config file path.
Read the mode and owner of each file.
Find the kube-proxy kubeconfig file, if kube-proxy uses one, and read its mode and owner.
Read the mode and owner of the files in the CNI configuration directory.
Make sure no user other than root can write to these files.
tests.ex: stat -c "%a %U:%G %n" /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/* /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml /etc/cni/net.d/*
tests.exp: Each file has the mode 600 or stricter, or 644 for the kubelet config file as the benchmark allows. The owner is root:root.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Worker node segmentation

tests.title: Check TLS settings and cipher suites of the API server
tests.obj: Finds API servers that accept weak TLS or have no client CA configured.
steps: Read the TLS certificate, TLS key and client CA flags of the API server.
Read the cipher suite and minimum TLS version settings.
Scan the API server port with a TLS scanner.
Make sure the secure port is not off and TLS 1.2 or 1.3 is the lowest version accepted.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep -E "tls|client-ca|secure-port"; nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 6443 <api-host>
tests.exp: The API server uses a TLS certificate and key, a client CA file and only strong cipher suites. TLS 1.2 is the lowest version.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Encryption

tests.title: Check TLS trust between the API server, etcd and the kubelets
tests.obj: Finds API servers that do not check or authenticate etcd and kubelet connections.
steps: Read the etcd CA, etcd client certificate and etcd client key flags of the API server.
Read the kubelet client certificate, kubelet client key and kubelet CA flags.
Make sure the etcd and kubelet connections use TLS and check the server certificate.
Make sure the kubelet CA is the cluster CA and not a bundle of public CAs.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep -E "etcd-(ca|cert|key)file|kubelet-(certificate|client)"
tests.exp: The API server connects to etcd and to the kubelets with client certificates. It checks the server certificate against a dedicated CA.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Encryption

tests.title: Check service account key and token settings of the API server
tests.obj: Finds API servers that accept tokens of deleted service accounts or give tokens long life.
steps: Read the service account key file, signing key and lookup flags of the API server.
Make sure service account lookup is on, so deleted accounts lose their tokens.
Read the token lifetime and the token expiry extension setting.
Make sure the ServiceAccount admission plugin is on.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep -E "service-account|admission"
tests.exp: The API server has a service account key file and lookup on. Token lifetime extension is off and the ServiceAccount admission plugin is on.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Authentication and authorization, Authentication

tests.title: Check flags of the controller manager, scheduler and kube-proxy
tests.obj: Finds control plane components that listen on all interfaces or share one identity.
steps: Read the bind address of the controller manager, the scheduler and the kube-proxy metrics service.
Read the profiling flag of the controller manager and the scheduler.
Read the service account credentials, root CA and signing key flags of the controller manager.
Read the terminated pod garbage collection threshold and the kubelet server certificate rotation setting.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-controller-manager -o yaml | grep -E "bind-address|profiling|use-service-account|root-ca|terminated"; ss -ltnp | grep -E "10257|10259|10249"
tests.exp: Components bind to 127.0.0.1 and profiling is off. The controller manager uses a separate credential for each controller and has a root CA file.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Control plane hardening

tests.title: Check API server profiling, timeout, event rate limit and insecure port
tests.obj: Finds API servers with debug endpoints, no request timeout or an open insecure port.
steps: Read the insecure port, profiling, request timeout and admission flags of the API server.
Try to connect to the insecure port from a control plane node.
Request a profiling path of the API server with an admin account.
Read the EventRateLimit configuration, if the plugin is on.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep -E "insecure|profiling|request-timeout|EventRateLimit"; kubectl get --raw /debug/pprof/
tests.exp: The insecure port is closed and profiling is off. A request timeout is set. Event rate limits are set where the plugin is in use.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Control plane hardening

tests.title: Check the NodeRestriction, AlwaysPullImages and DenyServiceExternalIPs plugins
tests.obj: Finds clusters where a node or a user can reach outside its own scope.
pre: Do not run on production.
steps: Read the enabled admission plugins of the API server.
Make sure NodeRestriction, AlwaysPullImages and DenyServiceExternalIPs are on, or an equal policy exists.
In a test namespace, create a Service that sets externalIPs.
With a kubelet credential in a test cluster, try to change the labels of another node.
tests.ex: kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-apiserver -o yaml | grep enable-admission-plugins; kubectl apply -f svc-externalips.yaml
tests.exp: NodeRestriction limits each kubelet to its own node and pods. New Services cannot set externalIPs. Image pulls are checked for each pod start.

tests.title: Check kubelet runtime settings for timeouts, PIDs, kernel and events
tests.obj: Finds kubelet settings that weaken node protection or hide events.
steps: Read the kubelet config file of a sample node.
Read the streaming connection idle timeout and the event record rate.
Read the pod PID limit, the protect kernel defaults setting and the iptables management setting.
Make sure the hostname override flag is not in use.
Make sure the default seccomp profile setting is on.
tests.ex: kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/configz" | jq .kubeletconfig | grep -Ei "streaming|podPidsLimit|protectKernel|iptables|eventRecord|seccompDefault"
tests.exp: Streaming timeouts are not zero and a pod PID limit is set. The kubelet protects kernel defaults, manages iptables and records events.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Resource policies

tests.title: Check kubelet TLS, client CA, cipher suites and certificate rotation
tests.obj: Finds kubelets with weak TLS, no client CA or no certificate rotation.
steps: Read the TLS certificate, TLS key and client CA settings of the kubelet.
Read the TLS cipher suite list of the kubelet.
Make sure client and server certificate rotation are on.
Scan port 10250 of a node with a TLS scanner.
tests.ex: nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 10250 <node-ip>; kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/configz" | jq .kubeletconfig.tlsCipherSuites
tests.exp: The kubelet uses a TLS certificate, a client CA and only strong cipher suites. It rotates its client and server certificates.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Network separation and hardening, Encryption

tests.title: Check add-ons and ingress controllers for known CVEs and end of life
tests.obj: Finds add-ons with known flaws or without security fixes.
steps: List the ingress controllers, GitOps tools and dashboards in the cluster with versions.
Compare each version to the vendor advisories and the end of life dates.
On ingress-nginx, make sure snippet annotations are off or the version is fixed.
Check the aggregated API servers and the Kubernetes version for open advisories.
tests.ex:
kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath="{..image}" | tr " " "
" | sort -u; kubectl -n ingress-nginx get cm -o yaml | grep allow-snippet
tests.exp: No add-on runs a version with a known critical flaw or past end of life. Snippet annotations of the ingress controller are off.

other: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance 1.2, section Upgrading and application security practices

tests.title: Check static pod paths and manifest sources of kubelets
tests.obj: Finds nodes where a local user or a web source can start pods that skip the API checks.
pre: Shell access to a worker node.
steps: Read the static pod path and static pod URL settings of the kubelet on each node.
Make sure the setting is off where a node does not need static pods.
List the files in the static pod directory and the mode of the directory.
Compare the pods in the runtime on the node to the pods in the API.
tests.ex: grep -E "staticPodPath|staticPodURL" /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml; ls -la /etc/kubernetes/manifests; crictl pods
tests.exp: Static pods are off or limited to known manifests in a protected directory. Each pod in the node runtime is visible in the API.

tests.title: Check access to the container runtime socket on nodes
tests.obj: Finds nodes where non-admin users can reach the runtime and start containers.
pre: Shell access to a worker node.
steps: Find the runtime socket paths on a node.
Read the mode, owner and group of each socket.
List the users and groups that can open the sockets.
Make sure the kubelet is isolated from other node services.
tests.ex: ls -l /run/containerd/containerd.sock /var/run/crio/crio.sock; getent group docker
tests.exp: Only root and the runtime group can use the runtime socket. Node login and superuser access are limited to named administrators.

tests.title: Check feature gates and API versions that are alpha or beta
tests.obj: Finds cluster features that are still in development and may carry flaws.
steps: List the feature gates of the API server, the kubelet and the controller manager.
Find gates that enable alpha or beta features.
Ask the owner what each feature does for the business.
Disable the features that are not in use.
