steps: Change a field in the test user profile with the self-service function.
Send a correction request for a field that the user cannot change directly.
Record the time until the service corrects the field or gives a refusal.
Check that processors and third parties hold the corrected value.
Check that the refusal states a valid reason.
tests.ex: Compare the field in the web application, the database and the processor export before and after the request.
tests.exp: The service corrects the data as soon as possible or tells the user of the refusal within 72 hours. Recipients receive the correction.

tests.title: Test the deletion request and the 72-hour limit
tests.obj: Finds deletion requests that are late, partial or refused with no reason.
pre: A test user whose data is in scope as data of a Vietnamese citizen.
Written permission to send data subject requests.
steps: Send a deletion request for the test user for data that is no longer needed.
Record the time until the service deletes the data.
Look for the data in the database, the search index, the file store and the processor systems.
Send a deletion request for data that the service must keep by law.
Check that the service tells the user why it did not delete.
tests.ex: Use the grounds in Decree Art. 16(1): no longer needed, consent withdrawn, objection, unlawful processing.
tests.exp: The service deletes all copies of the requested data within 72 hours. It states the legal ground when it refuses.

tests.title: Check that deletion is irrecoverable and covers old devices
tests.obj: Finds deleted data that an attacker can restore, or old media that still hold data.
steps: Delete a test record and then look for it in backups, snapshots and replicas.
Look for recovery tools or an undelete function in the application.
Review the way the organisation destroys disks and devices that held personal data.
Look at the record of the security check made before a device is wiped or destroyed.
tests.ex: Review the media destruction records and the retention schedule of backups. Try a database undelete or point-in-time restore on a test copy.
tests.exp: Deleted data cannot be restored by normal means. The organisation checks the security of a system before it wipes or destroys devices.

tests.title: Test the restriction of processing within 72 hours
tests.obj: Finds requests to restrict processing that the service ignores or does late.
pre: A test user whose data is in scope as data of a Vietnamese citizen.
Written permission to send data subject requests.
steps: Send a restriction request for chosen data of the test user.
Record the time until the service applies the restriction.
Check that analytics, e-mail and batch jobs do not use the restricted data.
Check that processors receive the restriction.
Check that the user can lift the restriction.
tests.ex: Look for a restriction flag in the data model. Run the marketing and reporting jobs and check their output.
tests.exp: The service restricts all requested data within 72 hours and stops all use except storage. Processors apply the restriction.

tests.title: Test the objection to disclosure and marketing within 72 hours
tests.obj: Finds objections that the service does not apply, or applies late.
pre: A test user whose data is in scope as data of a Vietnamese citizen.
Written permission to send data subject requests.
steps: Send an objection to use for advertising and marketing for the test user.
Send an objection to disclosure of the personal data to others.
Record the time until the service applies each objection.
Send a marketing e-mail campaign and check that the test user is not in it.
Check that partners stop to use the data.
tests.ex: Use the in-product opt-out and a written request. Check the suppression list.
tests.exp: The service applies the objection within 72 hours. The user gets no marketing and the data is not disclosed.

tests.title: Check the security measures for personal data across its life
tests.obj: Finds processing with no managed and technical protection from the start.
steps: Read the data protection rules of the organisation.
Check the list of managed and technical measures for each system.
Check that measures exist from the start of the project and are reviewed.
Check that standard-based controls are in use.
tests.ex: Review the policy, the control list and the last review date. Match with the security tests in the sheets SEC and WEB-DATA.
tests.exp: Managed and technical measures exist from the start and through the whole processing. The organisation reviews and updates them.

tests.title: Check the system log of personal data processing
tests.obj: Finds processing that leaves no trace for audit.
steps: Read the log design for systems that process personal data.
Do a read, change and delete action on a test record.
Find the log entries for each action.
Check the retention and protection of the log.
tests.ex: Search the log store by test user ID. Check the fields: who, when, what.
tests.exp: The system logs the processing of personal data and keeps the log. The log holds no clear personal data that it does not need.

tests.title: Test the system against unlawful collection of personal data
tests.obj: Finds interfaces that allow bulk scraping of personal data.
pre: Written permission to run request floods against the test system.
steps: List public pages and API endpoints that return personal data.
Send many requests for different user IDs from one client.
Check for rate limits, authentication and bot controls.
Check that the response shows only needed fields.
tests.ex: Burp Intruder or a script with 500 requests. Look at status codes and alerts.
tests.exp: The service blocks bulk collection of personal data from its systems and shows only needed fields.

tests.title: Check that partner data feeds are not a sale of data
tests.obj: Finds partner feeds that count as a purchase or sale of personal data.
steps: List the partner feeds and the data they carry.
Read the contracts for payment or exchange of personal data.
Check the legal ground and the consent for each feed.
Check that data is not offered for sale in any other channel.
tests.ex: Document review of partner contracts and the data catalogue. grep the code for export jobs.
tests.exp: No feed sells or buys personal data. Each transfer to a third party has a legal ground.

tests.title: Check that de-identified data cannot be traced back
tests.obj: Finds de-identified data sets that a party can link back to a person.
steps: Read the method to de-identify data.
Try to link the de-identified set with other sets that the organisation holds.
Check who holds the key or the mapping table.
Check the controls over the de-identification process.
tests.ex: Try a join on quasi-identifiers: date of birth, postcode, device ID. Review the key store.
tests.exp: A party cannot link de-identified data to a person. The process has access control and monitoring, and nobody re-identifies the data.

tests.title: Check access control and identity for AI, big data and cloud systems
tests.obj: Finds systems with weak authentication or roles around personal data.
steps: List the AI, big data, cloud and blockchain systems that use personal data.
Check the authentication method and the roles.
Check that the system uses personal data only for its stated purpose.
Check that the system has security measures built in.
tests.ex: Review the role matrix and the identity settings. Link to the sheets CLD, LLM and PRIV-SEC.
tests.exp: The system uses suitable authentication and role-based access for personal data, and it keeps within the stated purpose.

tests.title: Find sensitive personal data in the data inventory
tests.obj: Finds sensitive data that the inventory does not mark and therefore misses extra controls.
steps: Read the data inventory and the database schema.
Mark fields that fit the sensitive categories: health, biometric, location, bank and account data, race, religion, politics.
Look for such data in logs, files and analytics events.
Check that the inventory shows each sensitive field.
tests.ex: grep the schema for health, biometric, geo, account and card terms. Compare with the inventory.
tests.exp: All sensitive fields are in the inventory and are marked. No sensitive field is hidden in free text, logs or analytics.

tests.title: Check that the user is told when sensitive data is processed
tests.obj: Finds sensitive data processing that the user does not know about.
steps: Open each form that collects sensitive data.
Look for a clear message that the data is sensitive personal data.
Look for the same message in the consent text.
Check that the controller has a department or person named for data protection.
tests.ex: Screenshot the form and the consent text. Look for the notice before submit.
tests.exp: The user sees a notice that the data is sensitive before the service processes it. A data protection department or person is named.

tests.title: Test the age check and the parent consent for child data
tests.obj: Finds child data processing that starts with no age check or parent consent.
pre: A test account flow for child users.
Written permission to create test child profiles.
steps: Register as a user who states an age under 16 and one who states age 7 to 15.
Look for an age check before the service processes data.
Check that consent comes from the parent or guardian and, for age 7 or older, from the child as well.
Try to skip the parent step.
tests.ex: Burp Repeater: change the age or the consent flag in the registration request. Look at server-side checks.
tests.exp: The service checks the age before it processes data of a child. It needs consent of the guardian, and of the child from age 7.

tests.title: Test the stop and deletion of child data on request
tests.obj: Finds child data that stays after a guardian withdraws consent or an authority asks.
steps: Withdraw the consent of the guardian for a test child account.
Check that the service stops the processing.
Check that the service deletes the child data in a way that cannot be restored.
Check the process for a written request from an authority.
tests.ex: Look at the child account, backups and processor copies after the withdrawal.
tests.exp: The service stops processing child data and deletes it when the guardian withdraws consent or the purpose ends. It acts on a valid authority order.

tests.title: Check the handling of location data
tests.obj: Finds tracking of position with no consent or with access by other parties.
steps: Install the mobile application or open the web page that uses position.
Look for a notice about the use of location data.
Look for an option to switch tracking off.
Check network traffic for location sent to parties not related to the service.
tests.ex: Use a proxy to inspect traffic for latitude, longitude or Wi-Fi data. Check the OS permission prompt.
tests.exp: The service tracks position only with consent or by legal order. It tells the user, offers options and sends location to no unrelated party.

tests.title: Check the protection of biometric data
tests.obj: Finds biometric data that is stored or sent with weak physical, access or monitoring controls.
steps: List the places that store or send biometric data.
Check the physical security of the storage and the transport devices.
Check that only needed roles can read the data.
Look for monitoring and alerts on access to the data.
Check the notice to the user after harm.
tests.ex: Review the access list and the monitoring rules. Look for templates, images and raw samples.
tests.exp: The organisation limits access to biometric data, protects the storage devices and watches for abuse. It tells the user when harm occurs.

tests.title: Check the limits on sharing of health and insurance data
tests.obj: Finds health data that goes to insurers or care providers with no written request.
steps: List the recipients of health data.
Look for the legal ground or the written request of the user for each recipient.
Try to send data to an insurer without the request.
Check the contract clauses for reinsurance transfers.
tests.ex: Review data sharing agreements and interface logs between the health service and insurance partners.
tests.exp: Health data goes to care or insurance providers only after a written request of the user or an emergency. Reinsurance transfers are in the customer contract.

tests.title: Check the notice and retention of audio and video recordings
tests.obj: Finds recording with no notice or with data kept too long.
steps: Find the places and systems that record audio or video of people.
Look for a sign or notice that tells people about the recording.
Read the retention rule and the deletion job for the recordings.
Check that the use of the recordings fits the purpose.
tests.ex: Photograph the notice at the camera. Compare the oldest recording with the retention rule.
tests.exp: People can see that recording takes place. The system keeps recordings only as long as needed and deletes them after that.

tests.title: Check recruitment data and the monitoring of employees
tests.obj: Finds candidate data that is kept after the process, and secret monitoring of staff.
steps: Look at the data fields that the recruitment form requires.
Check that the data of rejected candidates is deleted, unless the candidate agreed to keep it.
Check that the service deletes employee data when the contract ends, unless the law or an agreement says otherwise.
Look for technical monitoring of staff and the notice to staff.
tests.ex: Review the HR system retention jobs and the staff notice. Compare the form fields with the job purpose.
tests.exp: The organisation asks only for data that the job needs and deletes it on time. Staff know about technical monitoring.

tests.title: Find all flows of data of Vietnamese citizens to other countries
tests.obj: Finds cross-border flows that are not on record.
steps: List the systems, cloud regions and platforms that process data collected in Vietnam.
Mark each system outside Vietnam, including remote access and remote support.
Use traffic capture to find data sent to foreign hosts.
Compare the result with the transfer register.
tests.ex: Use DNS and TLS SNI logs, cloud region settings and a proxy capture. Mark data of Vietnamese citizens by country code of the user.
tests.exp: The transfer register lists every flow of data of Vietnamese citizens to a place outside Vietnam, including foreign platforms that process the data.

tests.title: Review the content of the cross-border transfer impact assessment
tests.obj: Finds transfer assessments that miss required items.
steps: Get the transfer impact assessment dossier.
Check the details and contacts of the exporter and the importer.
Check the purpose, the data types, the safeguards and the risk assessment.
Check the consent of the data subject and the complaint process.
Check the written agreement between the exporter and the importer.
tests.ex: Use the six-item checklist from Decree Art. 25(2) as a table.
tests.exp: The dossier has all required items, including the written agreement of the exporter and the importer and the consent with a complaint process.

tests.title: Check the filing of the transfer dossier and the update schedule
tests.obj: Finds transfers that start with no filing or whose dossier is out of date.
steps: Find the date of the first transfer.
Check that the authority received an original dossier within 60 days of that date.
Check the update records after each change of the dossier content.
Look for a notice to the authority after the first transfer.
tests.ex: Document review: filing receipt, dossier version history, change log.
tests.exp: The dossier is filed within 60 days of the first transfer and each change is filed. The dossier is always ready for inspection.

tests.title: Check that the service can stop a transfer on order
tests.obj: Finds transfers that the operator cannot stop quickly when the authority orders it.
steps: Find the technical controls that start and stop each transfer.
Ask who can stop the transfer and how long it takes.
Try the stop on a test flow in the test environment.
Check that the operator keeps contact details for the authority and the responsible person.
tests.ex: Run the stop in the test environment: disable the export job, revoke the key or block the egress rule.
tests.exp: The operator can stop each cross-border transfer quickly on order and knows who does it.

tests.title: Check the cloud and platform settings for data of Vietnamese citizens
tests.obj: Finds cloud and SaaS tenants that send data abroad with no assessment.
steps: List the cloud and SaaS tenants that hold data of Vietnamese citizens.
Read the region and replication settings.
Check support access and logging exports.
Match each setting to the transfer dossier.
tests.ex: Cloud console region view, replication rules, log export targets.
tests.exp: Each tenant setting matches the transfer dossier. No replica or log copy leaves the stated location.

tests.title: Find all places where personal data leaves the legal region
tests.obj: Finds data transfers to other countries that nobody documented.
steps: List the regions of all hosts, backups, support tools and processors.
Check DNS and IP data of the hosts in application traffic.
Compare with the record of processing.
Mark each unrecorded transfer.
tests.ex: Cloud console region list; whois/geoip for hosts in the proxy log; record of processing activities.
tests.exp: All storage and processing locations are known. Each transfer outside the region is recorded.

tests.title: Check the legal mechanism for each transfer to a third country
tests.obj: Finds transfers with no adequacy decision or safeguard.
steps: List each third country and recipient.
Find the mechanism: adequacy decision, standard clauses or binding corporate rules.
Check the documents exist and are current.
Check the user notice names the safeguard.
tests.ex: Document review: transfer register with mechanism, date, contract reference.
tests.exp: Each transfer has a valid mechanism that is on record and named in the notice.

tests.title: Check the region settings of cloud and SaaS services
tests.obj: Finds services set to the wrong region or with global replication.
steps: Open the region and replication settings of each data store.
Check support and log tools for data copies in other regions.
Check that the settings match the record.
Check the infrastructure code for the same values.
tests.ex: Terraform or console review; look for global replication or default region values.
tests.exp: Region and replication settings match the recorded location. No uncontrolled copies exist elsewhere.

tests.title: Test the login for bypass by changing client state
tests.obj: Finds checks that only run in the client and that a user can change or skip.
steps: Find where the client decides that a user is logged in.
Change the local flag, config value or return value with a debugger.
Try to open a protected screen.
Send the server calls without the login step.
tests.ex: dnSpy breakpoint on the login method; Burp Suite replay of API calls with no token.
tests.exp: The server decides on access. A changed client flag does not give access to protected data or functions.

tests.title: Check that sessions end at logout, timeout and lock
tests.obj: Finds sessions and tokens that stay valid after the user leaves.
steps: Log in and note the session token or ticket.
Log out and replay the token against the server.
Leave the client idle and test again after the timeout.
Check the token files on disk after logout.
tests.ex: Burp Repeater or curl with the old token; Procmon on the profile folder.
tests.exp: The server rejects the old token. The client deletes local tokens. The idle timeout locks the client.

tests.title: Check hardware logins for a second factor
tests.obj: Finds RFID, smart card or USB key logins that work without a PIN.
steps: List the hardware factors that the client accepts.
Present a copied or lost device in a test setup.
Check if the client asks for a PIN or password.
Check the lock-out rules after wrong PINs.
tests.ex: Test device in a lab; check client logs for the PIN prompt and the count of failed tries.
tests.exp: A hardware device alone does not give access. The client asks for a PIN or password and locks after repeated failures.

tests.title: Check kiosk and shared-device modes for authentication gaps
tests.obj: Finds public or emergency modes that skip login and give too much access.
steps: List the modes that run without login.
Try to leave the kiosk shell with keys and dialogs.
Open file dialogs and help links.
List the data and functions reachable in each mode.
tests.ex: Keyboard shortcuts such as Alt+Tab and Ctrl+Alt+Del on a test machine; record each escape path.
tests.exp: Modes with no login expose only the planned functions. The user cannot reach the OS shell, files or admin functions.

tests.title: Check stored credentials and the remember-me feature
tests.obj: Finds saved passwords and tokens that others can read.
steps: Turn on remember me and log in.
Search the profile folder, registry and credential store for the secret.
Check file and key access rights.
Check the token life time.
tests.ex: Procmon filter on the client process; reg query HKCU\Software\Vendor; strings on profile files.
tests.exp: The client stores only a short-lived token in the OS credential store. It stores no password in clear or reversible form.

tests.title: Check install folders and config files for weak permissions
tests.obj: Finds files that low-privilege users can change.
steps: List the install folders and the data folders.
Read the access rights with icacls or ls -l.
Look for write rights for Users, Everyone or other.
Try to change a config file and a binary as a normal user.
tests.ex: icacls "C:\Program Files\Vendor" /T; accesschk.exe -uwdqs Users; find / -perm -o+w on Linux.
tests.exp: Only administrators can change program files. User data folders are readable only by the owner.

tests.title: Check the privilege level of the client and its services
tests.obj: Finds processes that run as administrator, root or SYSTEM without need.
steps: List all processes and services that the product installs.
Read the account of each process.
Check for setuid or setgid bits on Linux binaries.
Find which functions need elevation.
tests.ex: Process Explorer user column; sc qc service; find / -perm -4000 -user root.
tests.exp: Each process runs with the lowest rights it needs. No binary has setuid or setgid without need.

tests.title: Check registry keys and settings that carry security decisions
tests.obj: Finds registry values or policy files that a normal user can change to bypass controls.
steps: List the registry keys that the product reads and writes.
Check the access rights of each key.
Change a security setting as a normal user.
Restart the product and look at the effect.
tests.ex: Procmon filter on Registry operations; accesschk.exe -kvuqsw HKLM\Software\Vendor.
tests.exp: Only administrators can change security settings. A changed user-level value does not lower protection.

tests.title: Test admin functions of the client for vertical privilege change
tests.obj: Finds admin functions that the server allows for normal users.
steps: Log in as a normal user and as an admin.
Record the API calls for admin functions.
Replay them with the normal user token.
Show hidden menu items with a UI inspection tool.
tests.ex: Burp Suite Autorize extension; Snoop or Inspect.exe for hidden controls.
tests.exp: The server rejects admin calls from normal users. Hidden controls do not give access.

tests.title: Check code signing of the installer, binaries and libraries
tests.obj: Finds unsigned or wrongly signed files.
steps: List all executables and DLL files in the install.
Check the signature of each file.
Check that the certificate chain and time stamp are valid.
Change one file and start the product.
tests.ex: sigcheck.exe -u -e -s "C:\Program Files\Vendor"; Get-AuthenticodeSignature; codesign -v on macOS.
tests.exp: All shipped code has a valid signature from the vendor. A changed file is rejected by the installer or loader.

tests.title: Test for DLL search order hijacking and untrusted load paths
tests.obj: Finds loads of libraries from folders that a user can write.
steps: Run the product with Process Monitor.
Filter on NAME NOT FOUND for DLL loads.
Check the write rights of the searched folders.
Place a harmless test library in a writable searched folder.
tests.ex: Procmon filter: Result is NAME NOT FOUND and Path ends with .dll. Use a benign test DLL that writes a marker file.
tests.exp: The product loads libraries from fixed trusted paths. No searched folder is writable by normal users.

tests.title: Test temporary files and update steps for race conditions
tests.obj: Finds time-of-check time-of-use gaps in file handling.
steps: Find the temporary files and folders the product makes.
Check the names and the access rights.
Replace the file between check and use in a test setup.
Check that the product checks the file again.
tests.ex: Procmon file events; script that swaps a test file in a lab.
tests.exp: Temporary files have random names in a private folder. The product opens each file once and keeps the handle.

tests.title: Check binary hardening flags and memory safety of native code
tests.obj: Finds missing ASLR, DEP and stack protection and unsafe functions.
steps: List native binaries in the install.
Read the hardening flags of each.
Search for unsafe copy functions in the code or symbols.
Send over-long input to parsers in a test lab.
tests.ex: winchecksec; checksec --file on Linux; dumpbin /headers; fuzz parsers with a lab fuzzer.
tests.exp: All native binaries use ASLR, DEP and stack protection. Parsers check lengths and fail safely on long input.

tests.title: Check the release build for debug code and test data
tests.obj: Finds dead code, test accounts and debug switches in the release.
steps: Decompile the release build.
Search for debug flags, test accounts and test URLs.
Look for debug symbols and verbose log switches.
Start the client with a debug argument.
tests.ex: ILSpy; strings; command line flags such as --debug or environment variables in the code.
tests.exp: The release has no debug mode, test accounts or test data. Debug switches do not change security.

tests.title: Check that critical decisions do not depend on tamper detection alone
tests.obj: Finds license and admin checks that a debugger or hook can change.
steps: Attach a debugger to the client in a lab.
Hook the license or admin check with Frida.
Change the return value.
Check that the server confirms the result.
tests.ex: Frida script that only logs and changes one boolean in a test copy.
tests.exp: Critical decisions are made on the server. Hooking the client does not give paid or admin functions.

tests.title: Capture client traffic and find clear-text protocols
tests.obj: Finds HTTP, FTP, Telnet, MQTT or plain database traffic.
steps: Start Wireshark on the client interface.
Use all main functions.
List all protocols and ports in the capture.
Look for credentials and data in clear text.
tests.ex: Wireshark display filter !tls && !ssh; tshark -r cap.pcap -q -z conv,tcp.
tests.exp: All client traffic uses TLS or another encrypted protocol. No credentials or data appear in clear text.

tests.title: Check TLS versions and cipher suites of all client endpoints
tests.obj: Finds old protocol versions and weak ciphers.
steps: List all server hosts and ports from the capture.
Scan each endpoint for protocol versions and ciphers.
Check the database connection for TLS.
Compare with the approved list.
tests.ex: nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443,1433 host; testssl.sh host:port.
tests.exp: All endpoints accept only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 with strong ciphers.

tests.title: Test certificate validation in the client with an untrusted certificate
tests.obj: Finds clients that accept wrong, expired or self-signed certificates.
steps: Route the client through a proxy with its own CA.
Start the client without the CA in the trust store.
Watch if the client connects.
Repeat with an expired certificate and a wrong host name.
tests.ex: Burp Suite or mitmproxy with a fresh CA; look for certificate errors in the client log.
tests.exp: The client refuses all untrusted, expired and wrong-host certificates and sends no data.

tests.title: Check certificate pinning for critical hosts
tests.obj: Finds high-risk clients without a pin for the update or API host.
steps: Find the hosts that carry updates and credentials.
Look in the code for pin checks or custom validation callbacks.
Install a trusted proxy CA and try to read the traffic.
Make sure no callback returns true for all.
tests.ex: ILSpy search for ServerCertificateValidationCallback that returns true; Electron setCertificateVerifyProc.
tests.exp: The client pins keys for critical hosts or validates the full chain. No callback accepts every certificate.

tests.title: Check database connections for encryption and least privilege
tests.obj: Finds clients that use a shared database account over a plain channel.
steps: Find the connection string in the config or code.
Capture the database traffic.
Look for TLS in the handshake.
Check the rights of the database account.
tests.ex: Wireshark on port 1433, 3306 or 5432; SQL: SELECT * FROM fn_my_permissions(NULL,NULL).
tests.exp: The connection uses TLS. Each user or the service has an account with the least rights. The client holds no admin database account.

tests.title: Check named pipes, local ports and IPC for access control
tests.obj: Finds local interfaces that any user or any host can use.
steps: List named pipes, sockets and listening ports of the product.
Check the access rights of each pipe.
Check the bind address of each port.
Send a request as another local user.
tests.ex: pipelist.exe; accesschk.exe \pipe\name; netstat -ano; nmap -p- from a second host.
tests.exp: IPC objects allow only the needed accounts. Local services bind to loopback and need authentication.

tests.title: Check Windows services for unquoted paths and weak folder rights
tests.obj: Finds services that a user can hijack through the service path.
steps: List the services that the product installs.
Read the image path of each service.
Look for spaces in unquoted paths.
Check the write rights of each parent folder.
tests.ex: wmic service get name,pathname; sc qc; icacls on each folder in the path.
tests.exp: Service paths are quoted. No folder in the path is writable by normal users.

tests.title: Check file open and import functions for type and content checks
tests.obj: Finds file handlers that accept any file or parse unsafe content.
steps: List the file types the client opens or imports.
Open files with a wrong type and a wrong content.
Open files with an odd size and a long name.
Watch the client for crashes and file writes.
tests.ex: Procmon; WinDbg crash notes; test file set with a changed header.
tests.exp: The client checks file type and content before it parses the file. Bad files give a clear error and no crash.

tests.title: Check back-end services of the client for default credentials
tests.obj: Finds databases, queues and directory services with default accounts.
steps: List the back-end services that the client uses.
Read the connection settings in the config.
Try the vendor default account on a test instance.
Check the network rules around each service.
tests.ex: Look in the config for sa, root and admin accounts; nmap -sV on the service host.
tests.exp: Back-end services have no default accounts and allow access only from the client network.

tests.title: Check local-only features for exposure over the network
tests.obj: Finds services meant for the same machine that listen on all interfaces.
steps: List all listening sockets of the product.
Read the local address of each.
Connect from a second host.
Check the firewall rules that the installer adds.
tests.ex: netstat -ano | findstr LISTENING; Test-NetConnection from another host.
tests.exp: Local-only features bind to 127.0.0.1. The installer adds no inbound allow rule for them.

tests.title: Find weak or custom cryptography in the client
tests.obj: Finds weak algorithms, weak modes and home-made crypto code.
steps: Search the code for MD5, SHA1, DES, RC4, ECB and custom cipher classes.
List the calls to the crypto library.
Check the algorithm, key size and mode for each use.
Check that passwords use a password hashing function.
tests.ex: ILSpy search; grep for MD5, SHA1, DES and ECB; keyword list from WSTG-CRYP-04.
tests.exp: The client uses approved algorithms and modes and a maintained library. It uses no custom algorithm.

tests.title: Check that keys and salts are unique per installation
tests.obj: Finds keys, IVs and salts that are the same on every install.
steps: Install the client on two clean systems.
Compare the key files, key values and salts.
Find the code that makes keys and IVs.
Check the random source.
tests.ex: Binary diff of the two profile folders; ILSpy review for System.Random use.
tests.exp: Each install has its own keys from a secure random source. The client never reuses an IV or nonce with one key.

tests.title: Check key storage in the OS key store
tests.obj: Finds keys stored in clear form or in files next to the data.
steps: Find where the client keeps its keys.
Check if it uses DPAPI, the OS credential store or a hardware module.
Check the DPAPI scope, user or machine.
Check if the key and the data are in separate places.
tests.ex: ILSpy search for ProtectedData.Protect and DataProtectionScope.LocalMachine.
tests.exp: Keys are in an OS key store or hardware module with user scope. Keys are not next to the data in clear form.

tests.title: Check integrity protection of trusted local data
tests.obj: Finds files and license data that a user can change without detection.
steps: Find the local files that the client trusts.
Change one value in a test copy of the file.
Start the client.
Check that the client detects and rejects the change.
tests.ex: Hex editor on a test copy; compare the client behaviour with and without an HMAC.
tests.exp: The client protects trusted local data with a signature or HMAC and rejects a changed file.

tests.title: Search binaries and config files for hard-coded secrets
tests.obj: Finds keys, passwords and connection strings inside the installer and files.
steps: Install the client in a clean virtual machine.
Run strings and a secret scanner over all installed files.
Decompile managed code and search for keys and connection strings.
Test each found value for use.
tests.ex: strings -n 8 app.dll | grep -iE "pass|key|secret|conn"; gitleaks or trufflehog directory scan; ILSpy.
tests.exp: No secret is in any binary, config or resource. Each install gets its own credentials from a secret store.

tests.title: Check data at rest for clear text and weak access rights
tests.obj: Finds databases, caches and temporary files that hold sensitive data in clear form.
steps: Use the client with test data in each feature.
Watch file and registry writes with Procmon.
Open each written file and look for the test data.
Check the file permissions and the temporary folders.
tests.ex: Procmon filter Operation is WriteFile; icacls on the data folder; sqlite3 .dump on local databases.
tests.exp: Sensitive data is encrypted with a key that is not in the files. Only the user and the app can read the files.

tests.title: Check process memory after logout for sensitive data
tests.obj: Finds secrets and personal data that stay in memory after the session ends.
steps: Log in and open sensitive records.
Log out or lock the client.
Make a memory dump of the client process.
Search the dump for the test values and tokens.
tests.ex: procdump -ma app.exe dump.dmp; strings -el dump.dmp | grep -i testvalue; Frida memory scan on a lab host.
tests.exp: Secrets and sensitive records are cleared after use or logout. The dump does not hold them in readable form.

tests.title: Check logs, crash dumps and debug output for sensitive data
tests.obj: Finds tokens, passwords and personal data in logs and dumps.
steps: Use all main functions with default logging.
Cause an error and a crash.
Search log files, dump files and the event log for test values.
Check the folders and access rights.
tests.ex: Search the client log folder for password and token strings; Windows Event Viewer; Windows Error Reporting dump folder.
tests.exp: Logs and dumps hold no secrets or personal data. Debug output is off in the release.

tests.title: Check clipboard and recent-file lists for leaks
tests.obj: Finds sensitive data that the client copies to shared OS areas.
steps: Copy a sensitive field in the client.
Read the clipboard and the clipboard history.
Look at the recent-file lists and the thumbnails.
Look at the task switcher preview.
tests.ex: Windows clipboard history (Win+V); Get-Clipboard in PowerShell; recent items folder.
tests.exp: The client clears or limits clipboard data for secrets. Sensitive views are hidden in previews where the OS allows it.

tests.title: Build a component inventory and find known vulnerable versions
tests.obj: Finds outdated libraries, runtimes and frameworks.
steps: List all libraries, runtimes and frameworks in the install.
Make a software bill of materials.
Check each version against vulnerability databases.
Include transitive dependencies.
tests.ex: syft dir:. -o cyclonedx-json; grype sbom:./sbom.json; dependency-check; NVD search.
tests.exp: The inventory is complete. No component has a known high or critical vulnerability without a fix plan.

tests.title: Check bundled Electron, Chromium and runtime versions
tests.obj: Finds bundled engines that miss security fixes.
steps: Find the bundled runtime and web engine versions.
Compare them with the current supported versions.
Check the update process for engines.
Look for unsupported components.
tests.ex: About dialog; package.json; file properties of the runtime DLLs.
tests.exp: Bundled engines and runtimes are supported versions with current patches.

tests.title: Test the update mechanism for signed packages on a secure channel
tests.obj: Finds updates that a network attacker can replace.
steps: Find the update URL and the update file format.
Capture an update check.
Check that the channel uses TLS with certificate checks.
Serve a changed package from a lab server and look at the result.
tests.ex: mitmproxy in a lab; look for a signature check in the code before install.
tests.exp: The client installs only packages with a valid vendor signature. A changed package is rejected.

tests.title: Review the supported platforms and the patch policy of the vendor
tests.obj: Finds clients that need an unsupported OS or old runtime.
steps: Read the system requirements.
Find any OS or runtime that is out of support.
Ask for the patch time frames.
Look for an end-of-support notice for the product.
tests.ex: Document review: support matrix and patch policy.
tests.exp: The product runs on supported platforms. A patch policy with time frames exists.

tests.title: Test client input fields for SQL injection
tests.obj: Finds queries that the client builds from user input.
steps: List all input fields and file imports that reach a database.
Capture the database traffic or turn on the query log.
Send a single quote and a boolean test value in each field.
Compare the query text with the input.
tests.ex: Procmon or Wireshark on the database port; database general query log; sqlmap only against in-scope back ends.
tests.exp: The client uses parameterized queries. Special characters in input never change the query structure.

tests.title: Find OS command execution that uses user input
tests.obj: Finds calls to a shell or a process with input that the user controls.
steps: Search the code or decompiled code for process start calls.
Trace each call to its input source.
Send shell separators in the matching fields on a test system.
Watch child processes with Process Monitor.
tests.ex: ILSpy or dnSpy: search for Process.Start and ProcessStartInfo; Procmon filter on Process Create.
tests.exp: The client starts programs with a fixed path and separate arguments. No user value reaches a command interpreter.

tests.title: Check XML and import file parsers for external entities
tests.obj: Finds parsers that resolve external entities in untrusted files.
steps: List the file types and XML settings that the client reads.
Search the code for the parser settings.
Open a test file with an external entity that points to a canary file.
Look for an outbound request or a file read.
tests.ex: Canary file with a unique string; Procmon to watch file reads by the client process.
tests.exp: The parser turns off DTD and external entity resolution. Untrusted files cause an error and no file or network access.

tests.title: Check embedded HTML views for script injection
tests.obj: Finds web views and mail views that run script from untrusted content.
steps: Find the components that render HTML.
Load content with a harmless script marker in a test record.
Check if the marker runs.
Read the web view settings for script and file access.
tests.ex: Marker that only changes the page title; Electron or WebView2 settings review for nodeIntegration and contextIsolation.
tests.exp: Untrusted HTML is encoded or sanitized. The view runs no script and has no access to local files or system APIs.

tests.title: Check deserialization of files, messages and update data
tests.obj: Finds unsafe serializers that read data an attacker can change.
steps: Search the code for BinaryFormatter, ObjectInputStream and type name settings.
Find the data source of each call.
Look for serialized blobs in files and traffic.
Check the type allowlist or the signature check.
tests.ex: ILSpy search for BinaryFormatter and TypeNameHandling; look for the Base64 prefix AAEAAAD///// in saved files.
tests.exp: The client uses a data-only format such as JSON. It does not read objects whose type comes from the data stream.

tests.title: Check that security events are logged with who, when, where and what
tests.obj: Finds missing audit logs for login, access denial and admin actions.
steps: List the security events of the product.
Cause a failed login, a denied action and a config change.
Find the log entries.
Check each entry for user, time, source and action.
tests.ex: Windows Event Viewer; client log folder; event list from the Logging Cheat Sheet.
tests.exp: Each security event creates a log entry with user, time, source and action.

tests.title: Check access rights on log files and the audit trail
tests.obj: Finds logs that normal users can read or change.
steps: Find the log folders and files.
Read the access rights.
Try to edit and delete a log entry as a normal user.
Check for forwarding to a central system.
tests.ex: icacls on the log folder; compare local logs with the central copy.
tests.exp: Normal users cannot read or change audit logs. Logs go to a central system.

tests.title: Test log injection through user-supplied values
tests.obj: Finds log entries that a user can forge.
steps: Find input values that the client writes to logs.
Send a value with a line break and a made-up log entry.
Open the log file.
Check that the log shows the value as one encoded field.
tests.ex: Test value: a name followed by a line break and a made-up entry text.
tests.exp: Log writers encode or remove control characters. A user value cannot make a new log entry.

tests.title: Check that monitoring raises alerts for client abuse
tests.obj: Finds missing detection for repeated failed logins and tamper events.
steps: List the alert rules for the client and its back end.
Make 10 failed logins in a test.
Change a protected file in a test.
Check that alerts reach the responders.
tests.ex: SIEM rule list; test alert timestamps.
tests.exp: Abuse events create alerts that the responders receive within the agreed time.

tests.title: Make a component list from the firmware and find known vulnerabilities
tests.obj: Finds old kernels, libraries and daemons in the image.
steps: Unpack the firmware.
List the kernel, libc, web server, TLS library and other packages with versions.
Compare each version with vulnerability databases.
Record the fix status.
tests.ex: binwalk -e fw.bin; syft dir:_fw.bin.extracted; grype dir:_fw.bin.extracted; uname banner in the kernel.
tests.exp: No component has a known unpatched critical or high vulnerability. The vendor keeps a component list for each release.

tests.title: Check for unmaintained or unsupported components
tests.obj: Finds parts that no longer get fixes.
steps: List the end-of-life dates of the OS, kernel and libraries.
Mark unsupported items.
Check the replacement plan.
Check which items cannot be updated.
tests.ex: Document review plus version dates; compare with the vendor support policy.
tests.exp: No unsupported component is in use, or the vendor limits its exposure and plans its replacement.

tests.title: Review the supply chain of hardware and software parts
tests.obj: Finds untrusted suppliers and changed parts.
steps: List the chips, modules and third-party software.
Ask for the supplier security terms and patch ownership.
Compare the delivered part with the specification.
Check the code and hardware signing of the supplier.
tests.ex: Document review; hash compare of supplier firmware blobs with the vendor list.
tests.exp: Suppliers are assessed. Patch ownership and support periods are set in contracts. Delivered parts match the specification.

tests.title: Check OS hardening and process privileges on the device
tests.obj: Finds root-only designs, missing sandbox and weak file rights.
steps: Get a shell on a lab unit.
List the running processes and users.
Check file rights and writable system paths.
Check the kernel and OS hardening options.
tests.ex: ps; ls -l; find / -perm -4000; checksec --kernel; mount output for read-only flags.
tests.exp: Services run as non-root users with the least rights. System partitions are read-only where possible.

tests.title: Capture device traffic and find clear-text data
tests.obj: Finds data sent without encryption on any link.
steps: Capture traffic of the device on Wi-Fi, Ethernet and any radio.
List protocols and ports.
Look for credentials, tokens and data in clear text.
Check MQTT, CoAP and HTTP use.
tests.ex: Wireshark filter mqtt or coap or http; tshark -Y "http" -r cap.pcap.
tests.exp: All data in transit uses TLS, DTLS or an equal secure protocol. No credential or user data appears in clear text.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 5, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Test certificate validation and TLS settings of the device
tests.obj: Finds devices that accept any certificate or old TLS versions.
steps: Route device traffic through a proxy with a lab CA.
Check if the device connects.
Use an expired certificate and a wrong host name.
Scan the cloud endpoint for protocol versions.
tests.ex: mitmproxy with a lab CA; testssl.sh on the endpoint.
tests.exp: The device refuses untrusted certificates. Only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 with strong ciphers are used.

tests.title: Check sensitive data and keys in flash storage
tests.obj: Finds secrets and personal data stored in clear text on the device.
steps: Dump the flash of a lab unit.
Unpack the file systems.
Search for keys, tokens, Wi-Fi passwords and user data.
Check if the storage is encrypted.
tests.ex: flashrom -r dump.bin; binwalk -e dump.bin; strings; grep -r "BEGIN" _dump.bin.extracted.
tests.exp: Secrets and personal data are encrypted or kept in a secure element. No clear key is in the flash.

tests.title: Check cryptographic algorithms, key size and random source
tests.obj: Finds weak algorithms and poor random numbers.
steps: List the crypto libraries and calls in the firmware.
Check the algorithms, modes and key sizes.
Check the random source and its entropy at boot.
Check key use per device.
tests.ex: strings and Ghidra search for rand(), MD5, DES, ECB; ent on random output from a lab unit.
tests.exp: The device uses approved algorithms and a hardware or CSPRNG random source. Keys are unique per device.

tests.title: Check the logging of the device for sensitive data
tests.obj: Finds logs and diagnostic output with credentials or user data.
steps: Turn on default logging.
Use all main functions.
Read the logs from the console, files and cloud.
Search for secrets and personal data.
tests.ex: logread; dmesg; serial console capture; grep for token and password.
tests.exp: Logs hold no credentials or personal data. Diagnostic output is off or protected in production.

tests.title: Review the out-of-box configuration of the device
tests.obj: Finds insecure defaults such as open services, debug mode and weak encryption.
steps: Reset a lab unit to factory state.
Scan ports and read the default settings.
List all features that are on by default.
Compare with the minimum needed.
tests.ex: nmap -p- after reset; export of the default config.
tests.exp: Defaults are secure. Unneeded features are off, encryption is on and setup forces a new credential.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 12, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Check who can change security settings on the device
tests.obj: Finds devices that do not let operators harden them or that let users weaken them.
steps: List the security settings in the interface.
Change each setting as owner and as a limited user.
Check that a limited user cannot weaken them.
Check the audit entry for each change.
tests.ex: Web interface review; API calls with low-privilege tokens.
tests.exp: Operators can raise security settings. Only authorized roles can change them and each change is logged.

tests.title: Check that debug interfaces and test features are off in production
tests.obj: Finds enabled UART consoles, JTAG, test accounts and debug services.
steps: Open the case of a lab unit.
Find UART and JTAG pads.
Connect a logic adapter and watch the boot output.
Try to get a shell or debug access.
tests.ex: Identify pins with a multimeter; screen /dev/ttyUSB0 115200; OpenOCD on a lab unit only.
tests.exp: Production units give no shell or debug access on UART or JTAG without authentication. Debug services are off.

tests.title: Test secure boot and image signing
tests.obj: Finds devices that boot unsigned code.
steps: Read the boot chain description.
Write a changed image to a lab unit.
Boot the unit.
Check that the first stage is in ROM or locked.
tests.ex: Programmer or bootloader console on a lab unit; read the fuse state if documented.
tests.exp: Each boot stage checks the signature of the next. The device refuses to boot a changed image.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 7, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Check removable media and autorun behavior
tests.obj: Finds devices that run or import code from USB or SD cards.
steps: Insert a USB drive or SD card with a harmless marker script.
Watch the device.
Check import and update from media.
Check for signature checks on media content.
tests.ex: Marker script that only writes a file; serial console log.
tests.exp: The device does not run code from media. Updates from media need a valid signature.

tests.title: Test the device web interface for authentication and input flaws
tests.obj: Finds missing login, injection and XSS in the device web interface.
steps: Map every page and request of the web interface.
Call each admin request without a login.
Send special characters in each field.
Check the cookie and header settings.
tests.ex: Burp Suite; commix only in a lab for command injection checks.
tests.exp: Every request needs authentication and authorization. Input is validated. The interface has no injection flaw.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 13, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Test the cloud and back-end API used by the device
tests.obj: Finds API calls that expose other devices or users.
steps: Capture the API calls of the device and the app.
Change the device ID in each call.
Replay calls with a token from another account.
Check the responses for other data.
tests.ex: Burp Repeater; compare the responses for device A and device B.
tests.exp: The API checks that the caller owns the device. Changed IDs give an error and no data.

tests.title: Check the companion mobile app and the device for shared trust
tests.obj: Finds mobile app flows that let a user take control of a device they do not own.
steps: Pair a lab device with account A.
Try to pair or control it with account B.
Check the ownership change and reset steps.
Check what the old owner can still do.
tests.ex: Burp Suite on the app; Frida only on a lab device; the mobile app tests are in the MOB sheet.
tests.exp: Only the owner can control the device. An ownership change removes the access of the old owner.

tests.title: Check input validation and output filtering on all device interfaces
tests.obj: Finds interfaces that act on data without a check of type, length and range.
steps: List all input paths: API, radio, serial, file.
Send out-of-range and wrong-type values.
Check the state in which the action is allowed.
Check the output for internal data.
tests.ex: Protocol client scripts for MQTT, CoAP or HTTP; compare the responses.
tests.exp: The device checks type, length, range and state before it acts. Errors show no internal data.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 13, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Test command messages for replay and spoofing
tests.obj: Finds control messages that an attacker can copy and send again.
steps: Capture a command message such as lock or open.
Send it again later from another host.
Change a field and send it with the old signature.
Check for a counter or timestamp check.
tests.ex: Wireshark capture; scapy or mosquitto_pub replay in a lab.
tests.exp: The device rejects replayed, changed and unauthenticated commands.

tests.title: Check the device inventory and the remote management channel
tests.obj: Finds fleets that have no asset list and unauthenticated remote management.
steps: Ask for the device inventory process.
Find the remote management service.
Test the authentication on the channel.
Test whether one command reaches one device only.
tests.ex: Document review plus a lab connection to the management service with a test token.
tests.exp: The operator knows every device and its version. Remote management needs strong authentication and is logged.

tests.title: Check device monitoring, anomaly alerts and incident response
tests.obj: Finds fleets where attacks produce no alert.
steps: List the telemetry and logs the cloud receives.
Make a test event: failed logins and a config change.
Check that an alert fires.
Check the incident response contact for the product.
tests.ex: SIEM or cloud monitor rule list; test alert time.
tests.exp: Security events create alerts. A response plan and a vulnerability disclosure contact exist.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 2 and 10, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Test secure decommissioning and credential revocation
tests.obj: Finds retired devices that keep access to the cloud.
steps: Register a lab device.
Remove it in the cloud console.
Try to connect with its credentials.
Check that the device wipes local keys.
tests.ex: Replay the device token after removal; read the device storage after the wipe.
tests.exp: A removed device loses all cloud access at once. Local keys and data are wiped.

tests.title: Check behaviour of the device when the network or power fails
tests.obj: Finds devices that fail open or lose their security state.
steps: Cut the network on a lab unit.
Check local functions and security checks.
Cut and restore power.
Check that the device returns to a safe state.
tests.ex: Disconnect the uplink; power cycle with a controllable switch.
tests.exp: The device keeps its security settings. It fails safe and joins the network again in an orderly way.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 9, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Scan the device for open ports and unneeded services
tests.obj: Finds services that the device does not need, such as Telnet, FTP and debug daemons.
steps: Power the device on a lab network.
Scan all TCP and UDP ports.
List each service and its version.
Compare with the documented service list.
tests.ex: nmap -sS -sU -p- -sV --top-ports 1000 device; masscan on a lab range only.
tests.exp: Only documented services listen. Telnet, FTP and debug services are off. Each service needs authentication.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 6, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Check the services of the device for known vulnerable versions
tests.obj: Finds old daemons with public vulnerabilities.
steps: Read the version banner of each service.
Check each version in vulnerability databases.
Check for unpatched web server and UPnP builds.
Record the fixed version.
tests.ex: nmap -sV --script vulners device; compare with NVD.
tests.exp: No service version has a known unpatched vulnerability.

tests.title: Test the device for exposure to the internet
tests.obj: Finds devices that open ports to the internet through UPnP or default NAT rules.
steps: Check if the device asks the router to open ports.
Scan the public address of the lab network from outside.
Check for cloud relay use instead of inbound ports.
Record each reachable service.
tests.ex: upnpc -l on the lab network; external nmap scan of the lab WAN address.
tests.exp: The device opens no inbound port to the internet. Remote access uses an authenticated outbound cloud channel.

tests.title: Test network services with malformed input and long input
tests.obj: Finds crashes and memory errors in the parsers of the device.
steps: Pick one network service.
Send over-long and malformed fields in a lab.
Watch the device for crash, reboot or hang.
Record the input that caused it.
tests.ex: Boofuzz or a protocol fuzzer on a lab device; serial console log for crash traces.
tests.exp: The service rejects bad input with an error. The device does not crash or reboot.

tests.title: Check wireless interfaces for weak pairing and open access
tests.obj: Finds Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and radio links with weak pairing or no encryption.
steps: List all radio interfaces of the device.
Capture the pairing and the data with a sniffer.
Check the encryption and the pairing method.
Try to join without a user action.
tests.ex: Wireshark with a monitor mode adapter; Bluetooth sniffer; nRF Sniffer on a lab device.
tests.exp: Radio links use encryption and authenticated pairing. The device does not join or pair without a user action.

tests.title: Review the casing, ports and tamper protection of the device
tests.obj: Finds exposed ports and a casing that gives easy access to the board.
steps: List all external ports and buttons.
Open the casing.
Check for tamper switches and seals.
Check for labeled debug pads.
tests.ex: Visual inspection with a camera and a multimeter.
tests.exp: Unused ports are closed. The casing shows tamper evidence. Debug pads are removed or locked.

tests.title: Test flash and memory extraction
tests.obj: Finds devices where an attacker can read the firmware and secrets from the chip.
steps: Identify the flash chip.
Try an in-circuit read in a lab.
Check the dump for clear data.
Check read-out protection fuses.
tests.ex: flashrom with a clip programmer; binwalk on the dump.
tests.exp: Read-out protection or storage encryption stops the use of a dump. Secrets are not in clear text.

tests.title: Test the physical access of lost or captured devices to cloud accounts
tests.obj: Finds devices that give a finder access to the account or network.
steps: Take a lab device with a paired account.
Read stored tokens and Wi-Fi settings.
Use them from another host.
Check the revocation steps for the owner.
tests.ex: Extract the tokens from the lab dump; replay them against the lab cloud.
tests.exp: A stolen device does not give lasting access. The owner can revoke the device and its tokens.

tests.title: Check side channels and fault injection protection for high-risk devices
tests.obj: Finds secrets that leak through power analysis or glitches.
steps: Decide if the threat model includes lab attackers.
Check the secure element or crypto chip data sheet.
Check for glitch and temperature monitors.
Review any lab test report.
tests.ex: Document review: certification reports, chip data sheets.
tests.exp: Devices with high risk use certified secure elements. The vendor holds a test report.

tests.title: Map the personal data that the device and its cloud collect
tests.obj: Finds data that the device collects without need or without notice.
steps: Capture device, app and cloud traffic during normal use.
List all data types: audio, video, location, identifiers.
Compare with the privacy notice.
Mark data without a stated purpose.
tests.ex: Wireshark and mitmproxy in a lab; field list against the notice.
tests.exp: The device sends only data that is needed and named in the notice. Sensors do not record without a user signal.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 8, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Test removal of personal data at factory reset and transfer of ownership
tests.obj: Finds data that stays on a device after reset or sale.
steps: Fill a lab device with test user data.
Do a factory reset.
Read the flash with a programmer or from a shell.
Search the dump for the test data.
tests.ex: Dump flash with flashrom or a serial shell; strings and grep for test data.
tests.exp: A factory reset removes all personal data and credentials. Users get clear steps to delete data.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 11, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Check unique device identifiers and metadata for tracking
tests.obj: Finds identifiers that let others track users.
steps: Capture radio and cloud traffic.
Look for fixed MAC, serial and device ID values.
Compare the values over time and place.
Check what third parties receive.
tests.ex: Wireshark; Bluetooth sniffer for static addresses.
tests.exp: Identifiers are random or rotate where possible. Metadata is not shared without a stated need.

tests.title: Check consent, privacy controls and third-party sharing for the device
tests.obj: Finds sharing with partners without consent and no control for the user.
steps: Read the setup flow for consent steps.
Look for privacy settings in the app.
Capture traffic to third-party hosts.
Withdraw consent and capture again.
tests.ex: mitmproxy host list before and after consent change.
tests.exp: Users can give and withdraw consent. Sharing with third parties stops after withdrawal.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 8, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Find default and shared credentials on the device
tests.obj: Finds devices that ship with the same login on every unit.
steps: Read the quick start guide and the label for default logins.
Log in to each interface with the default login.
Reset two devices to factory state.
Compare the credentials of the two devices.
tests.ex: nmap -sV -p- device; hydra is not needed: try only the vendor documented login on a lab unit.
tests.exp: Each device has a unique credential or forces a new one at first use. A reset never restores a shared default.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 1, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Search the firmware for hard-coded passwords and keys
tests.obj: Finds credentials and backdoor accounts inside the firmware image.
steps: Get the firmware image from the vendor site or the device.
Unpack it with binwalk -e.
Search the files for passwd, shadow, keys and strings.
Test each found account on a lab device.
tests.ex: binwalk -e fw.bin; firmwalker.sh _fw.bin.extracted; strings -n 8 bin/* | grep -i pass; cat etc/shadow.
tests.exp: The firmware holds no hard-coded password, key or backdoor account. All secrets are made per device.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 4, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Test password policy and lock-out on the device interfaces
tests.obj: Finds weak passwords and unlimited guessing on web, SSH and Telnet.
steps: List every interface that accepts a password.
Set a short and a common password.
Send 20 wrong logins in a row to a lab unit.
Check for a delay, a lock or an alert.
tests.ex: Burp Intruder at low rate on the device web login; nmap --script ssh-auth-methods.
tests.exp: The device rejects weak passwords. Repeated wrong logins cause a delay or a lock.

tests.title: Check how the device stores and checks user passwords
tests.obj: Finds clear text and weak hashes in device databases.
steps: Find the password file or database in the extracted firmware.
Read the stored value format.
Identify the hash type and salt.
Check the hash cost.
tests.ex: cat etc/shadow; sqlite3 config.db .dump; look for crypt prefixes $1$, $5$, $6$, $y$.
tests.exp: Passwords are stored with a salted, slow hash such as Argon2id, bcrypt or PBKDF2.

tests.title: Check device-to-cloud identity and mutual authentication
tests.obj: Finds devices that share one cloud key or do not prove their identity.
steps: Capture the device enrollment.
Compare the device credentials of two units.
Present one device credential from another device in a lab.
Check that the cloud rejects the copy.
tests.ex: Wireshark and a lab proxy; compare client certificates or tokens of two devices.
tests.exp: Each device has its own identity. The cloud rejects a credential that comes from a different unit or is revoked.

tests.title: Check that firmware updates are signed and the device checks the signature
tests.obj: Finds devices that install unsigned or changed firmware.
steps: Get an update package.
Change one byte in a lab copy.
Try to install it.
Try to install a package with a wrong signature.
tests.ex: binwalk the package; openssl dgst -verify; flash the changed copy only on a lab unit.
tests.exp: The device rejects firmware with a missing or wrong signature.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 3, as listed in iot_map.md

tests.title: Test the update channel for transport protection
tests.obj: Finds update downloads over HTTP or TLS without certificate checks.
steps: Capture an update check and download.
Look at the protocol and the certificate checks.
Serve a lab response from a proxy.
Check what the device does.
tests.ex: mitmproxy with a lab CA; Wireshark.
tests.exp: The device gets updates over TLS with certificate validation. It rejects a proxy response.

tests.title: Test anti-rollback of firmware
tests.obj: Finds devices that accept older vulnerable firmware.
steps: Record the current firmware version.
Get an older signed package.
Try to install it in a lab.
Check the version counter in the bootloader.
tests.ex: Install an older signed image on a lab unit; read the version from the console.
tests.exp: The device refuses older firmware versions. A version counter in protected storage enforces this.

tests.title: Test interrupted updates and recovery
tests.obj: Finds devices that stay broken or unprotected after a failed update.
steps: Start an update on a lab unit.
Cut power at 50 percent.
Power on again.
Check the version, the state and the signature check.
tests.ex: Controllable power switch; serial console log.
tests.exp: The device boots a known good image or a signed recovery image. It never runs half-written code.

tests.title: Check update notices and the published support period
tests.obj: Finds products with no update notice or published end of support.
steps: Find the update notice in the app or the device.
Read the support period in the documentation.
Check the update steps for a normal user.
Check the notice for the reason of the update.
tests.ex: Document review: support policy, release notes, update UI.
tests.exp: Users see update notices with the reason. The vendor publishes a minimum support period.

other: UK Code of Practice for Consumer IoT Security provision 3, as listed in iot_map.md
